definition_zh: 宗教的；虔诚的；一丝不苟的
definition_en: connected with religion, or believing strongly in a religion
core_image: 每天同一时刻点灯、同一方向叩拜的人
scene: 寺院的钟声一响，山下的居民就放下手里的活，走进那座古老的建筑。 When the temple bell rang, the villagers stopped their work and walked into the old religious building.
sceneCN: 这里 religious 是「宗教的」（第 1 个义项：与宗教有关的）；句意：寺院的钟声一响，村民们停下手里的活，走进那座古老的宗教建筑。

pos.zh: 宗教的；虔诚的；一丝不苟的

derivatives.zh: religious 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地；一丝不苟地」
religious 的名词来源，义为「宗教」
加否定前缀 ir- 构成，义为「不虔诚的；无宗教信仰的」

senses.title: Connected with religion
senses.definition: relating to religion, its beliefs, or its practices
senses.definitionCN: 与宗教、其信仰或仪式有关的
senses.example: The building is used for religious ceremonies.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑用于宗教仪式。
senses.why: The adjective is simply the noun religion with a Latin ending added, so it describes anything that belongs to that binding system.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是名词 religion 加上拉丁词尾，因此描述一切属于那套系缚体系的东西。

senses.title: Believing strongly in a faith
senses.definition: believing firmly in a religion and taking part in its practices regularly
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地信仰某种宗教并规律参与其仪式
senses.example: Her grandmother was a deeply religious woman.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖母是一位非常虔诚的女性。
senses.why: A person held tightly by the bond of faith is described with the same adjective, which shifts from belonging to devotion.
senses.whyCN: 被信仰之绳牢牢系住的人也用同一个形容词描述，词义从「属于」转向「虔诚」。

senses.title: Done with great care and regularity
senses.definition: done carefully and at fixed times, as if it were a duty
senses.definitionCN: 认真且按固定时间去做，仿佛是一项义务
senses.example: He checks the figures with religious care.
senses.exampleCN: 他以近乎虔诚的仔细核对数字。
senses.why: Someone who never misses a rite becomes the model for anyone who never misses a routine.
senses.whyCN: 从不缺席仪式的人，成了从不漏掉任何例行事务之人的范本。

intro.en: Religious is the Latin-derived adjective of religion, formed with the ending -ous.
intro.cn: religious 是由 religion 派生、带拉丁词尾 -ous 的形容词。

items.en: Religiosus describes someone careful about rites and full of scruple.
items.cn: religiosus 形容对仪式谨慎、心存顾忌的人。

items.en: The suffix -osus means full of, so religiosus means full of religious care.
items.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 意为「满怀宗教式谨慎的」。

items.en: Old French religieus keeps both the belonging sense and the devout sense.
items.cn: 古法语 religieus 同时保留「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两层意思。

items.en: English religious first names members of a monastic order.
items.cn: 英语中的 religious 最初指修会成员。

items.en: The adjective widens to cover anything connected with faith and, figuratively, any careful routine.
items.cn: 这个形容词后来扩展到一切与信仰有关的事物，并比喻性地指任何谨慎的例行做法。

note.en: Religious is the everyday adjective of the religion family, and it stands near words for devotion and for belief.
note.cn: religious 是 religion 词族中日常使用的形容词，并与表示虔诚和信念的词相邻。

entries.definition: belief in a god or gods and its system of worship
entries.definitionCN: 宗教；宗教信仰，是 religious 的名词来源

entries.definition: in a very careful and regular way
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚地；一丝不苟地，由 religious 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: showing no interest in or respect for religion
entries.definitionCN: 不虔诚的；漠视宗教的，由否定前缀 ir- 构成

entries.definition: very religious and sincere in belief
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的，语气比 religious 更强

entries.definition: showing deep respect for God and religion
entries.definitionCN: 虔诚的；恭敬的，有时带做作之意

entries.definition: relating to the human spirit rather than the body
entries.definitionCN: 精神的；心灵的，不必然属于宗教

normalIntro.en: Religious is just religion plus the Latin ending -ous, so the hooks mostly revisit the noun.
normalIntro.cn: religious 就是 religion 加上拉丁词尾 -ous，所以记忆钩子大多回到那个名词。

normal.en: Drop the noun ending and add -ous: religion becomes religious.
normal.cn: 去掉名词词尾，加上 -ous，religion 就变成 religious。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get religiously, which also means doing something without fail.
normal.cn: 再加 -ly 得到 religiously，它也表示从不间断地做某事。

normal.en: Add the negative prefix ir- for irreligious, the opposite of devout.
normal.cn: 加否定前缀 ir- 得到 irreligious，与虔诚相反。

normal.en: Deeply religious is a very common pairing in both speech and writing.
normal.cn: deeply religious 是口语和书面语中都很常见的搭配。

normal.en: The family also contains religion and religiosity, all built on the same root.
normal.cn: 这个词族还包括 religion 和 religiosity，都建立在同一词根上。

abstract.en: Picture a person who lights the same lamp at the same hour every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人每天同一时刻点亮同一盏灯。

abstract.en: See hands folded and eyes lowered in a quiet room.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的房间里合起的手与低垂的眼。

abstract.en: Think of someone checking a list three times, as if it were a rite.
abstract.cn: 想一个人把清单核对三遍，仿佛在行仪式。

examples.en: The festival has both a religious and a social side.
examples.cn: 这个节日既有宗教的一面，也有社交的一面。

examples.en: She comes from a very religious family.
examples.cn: 她来自一个非常虔诚的家庭。

examples.en: He follows the training plan with religious discipline.
examples.cn: 他以近乎虔诚的自律执行训练计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽哲思」——想象瑞丽小城里有人整日哲思信仰；只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 religiosus（对仪式谨慎、心存敬畏），源自 religio；词尾 -osus 表示「充满」。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts as a label for things belonging to faith and widens to describe a devout person and then any careful routine.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词起初标记属于信仰的事物，随后扩展到形容虔诚的人，再扩展到任何一丝不苟的例行做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person who keeps the same rite at the same hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：每天同一时刻行同一仪式的人。

branches.en: Anything tied to the faith is labelled with the adjective.
branches.cn: 一切与信仰相关的事物都用这个形容词标记。

branches.en: A person held by the bond is called devout rather than merely belonging.
branches.cn: 被这根绳索系住的人，就从「属于」转为「虔诚」。

branches.en: Never missing a rite becomes the model for never missing a routine.
branches.cn: 从不缺席仪式，成为从不漏掉例行事务的范本。

branches.en: The belonging sense and the devout sense grow from the same root.
branches.cn: 「属于宗教」与「虔诚」两义出自同一词根。

branches.en: Both stress regularity in the service of something held sacred.
branches.cn: 两者都强调为某种被视为神圣之物而保持的规律性。

intro.en: Religious keeps the Latin root of religion and adds an adjective ending.
intro.cn: religious 保留 religion 的拉丁词根，并加上形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The ending -osus means full of, so religiosus describes a person full of religious care.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -osus 表示「充满」，因此 religiosus 形容满怀宗教式谨慎的人。

items.example: The relig- root is shared with religion.
items.exampleCN: relig- 词根与 religion 共用。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The ending -ous turns a noun into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 把名词变成形容词。

items.example: Irreligious uses ir- before the letter r.
items.exampleCN: irreligious 在字母 r 前使用 ir-。

items.example: Religiosus is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: religiosus 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.example: Religio supplies the stem of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: religio 提供这个形容词的词干。

items.example: Religiosity adds -ity to the same stem.
items.exampleCN: religiosity 在同一词干后加了 -ity。

items.meaning: connected with God and treated with great respect
items.example: Sacred is a near partner of religious in meaning.
items.exampleCN: sacred 在语义上是 religious 的近邻。

derivatives.zh: 不虔诚的；无宗教信仰的

definition_zh: 酒馆；酒吧；（澳新）旅店
definition_en: a building or room where alcoholic drinks are served and drunk, especially in Britain; also, in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel with a bar
core_image: 傍晚街角亮起暖灯的小店，木门一推开就是碰杯声
scene: 下班铃响过，几个人把工具袋往肩上一搭，拐进街角那家挂着旧木牌的小店。 After the shift, the crew walked down to the pub on the corner for a quick drink.
sceneCN: 这里 pub 是「酒馆」（第 1 个义项：英国供人坐下喝酒的场所）；句意为下工之后，工人们走到街角那家酒馆喝一杯。图中可辨识物件：旧木牌、暖灯、吧台。

derivatives.zh: 与 public 同源、经营酒馆的人；英式英语指酒馆老板，拉丁语原义是包税人
pub 与 crawl 复合，指一晚连喝好几家酒馆
pub 加表示「常去者」的 -goer，指常泡酒馆的人

senses.title: A place where alcoholic drinks are served
senses.definition: a building or room, especially in Britain, where people sit and buy alcoholic drinks to drink there
senses.definitionCN: 尤指英国的建筑或房间，人们坐在里面买酒并当场饮用
senses.example: We met in a quiet pub behind the station.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在车站后面一家安静的酒馆碰了头。
senses.why: Pub is public house cut short, and a public house was simply a house open to the public for drink, so the short form still names a room anyone may walk into.
senses.whyCN: pub 是 public house（向公众开放的房子）的截短，而 public house 本就是指「对公众开放、可以进去喝酒的房子」，所以短词仍指谁都能推门进去的那间屋子。

senses.title: A hotel with a bar in Australia and New Zealand
senses.definition: in Australia and New Zealand, a hotel that has a bar and often also serves meals and lets rooms
senses.definitionCN: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，指带酒吧的旅店，常兼供饭食并出租房间
senses.example: They stayed two nights at the pub beside the highway.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在公路边那家旅店住了两晚。
senses.why: On the long colonial roads one building sold drink, cooked meals and let a bed, so the word for the drinking room widened to cover the whole hotel.
senses.whyCN: 在漫长的殖民时期公路边，一栋房子同时卖酒、做饭、租床位，于是原本指饮酒房间的词扩大到了整间旅店。

senses.title: The local pub as a neighbourhood meeting place
senses.definition: the nearby pub understood as a regular social centre where neighbours meet and exchange news
senses.definitionCN: 把附近那家酒馆看作固定聚点，邻居在那里见面、交换消息
senses.example: The village pub is where everyone hears the news first.
senses.exampleCN: 村里那家酒馆是所有人最先听到消息的地方。
senses.why: The same room serves the same street every evening, so a business turns into the place where a neighbourhood talks, and English lets the old word carry that role too.
senses.whyCN: 同一间屋子每晚招待同一条街的人，一门生意便变成了街坊说话的地方，英语让这个旧词一并承担这重角色。

senses.title: Of or happening in a pub, used before a noun
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean served, held, or happening in a pub
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一个名词前，表示「酒馆供应的、酒馆里举办的」
senses.example: Sunday pub lunches are a habit in this town.
senses.exampleCN: 周日去酒馆吃午饭是这个镇上的习惯。
senses.why: Once pub names a place, it can stand in front of another noun and mark that thing as belonging to the place, which is exactly how pub food and pub quizzes are formed.
senses.whyCN: pub 一旦指某个场所，就能站到另一个名词前面，标明那样东西属于这个场所，pub food 与 pub quiz 正是这样构成的。

intro.en: Pub is not inherited from Latin but clipped from the English phrase public house in the nineteenth century; the public part of that phrase goes back to Latin publicus, from populus, the people.
intro.cn: pub 并非直接从拉丁语继承而来，而是十九世纪从英语短语 public house 截短而成；其中 public 可上溯到拉丁语 publicus，而 publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

items.en: Populus meant the people taken as one body, and it is the root behind the adjective publicus.
items.cn: populus 意为作为整体的人民，是形容词 publicus 背后的词根。

items.en: Publicus meant belonging to the people or the state, that is, open to all citizens rather than held privately.
items.cn: publicus 意为「属于人民或国家的」，也就是向全体公民开放、而非私人占有。

items.en: From the later seventeenth century English called an inn or tavern a public house, a house open to the public for eating and drinking.
items.cn: 十七世纪后期起，英语把客栈、酒馆称作 public house，即向公众开放、供人饮食的房子。

items.en: In the nineteenth century, first in British working speech, the phrase was cut down to the single syllable pub, and the short form spread quickly.
items.cn: 十九世纪，先是英国劳工阶层口语把这个短语截成单音节 pub，短形式很快传开。

items.en: Modern English uses pub for the British drinking place, for the Australian hotel, and inside compounds such as pub quiz, pub food and pub-crawl.
items.cn: 现代英语用 pub 指英国的饮酒场所、澳新的旅店，也用在 pub quiz、pub food、pub-crawl 这类复合词里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the phrase pub was cut from and its Latin relatives; the near-meaning group gathers other words for places that sell drink.
note.cn: 形近组收 pub 被截短之前的短语与它的拉丁同族词；近义组收其他表示卖酒场所的词。

entries.definition: The full form that pub was cut from: a house open to the public for food and drink.
entries.definitionCN: pub 被截短之前的完整形式：向公众开放、供饮食的房子。

entries.definition: In British English the keeper of a pub; the Latin word once meant a tax farmer.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中指酒馆老板；这个拉丁词原本指包税人。

entries.definition: Open to all people, or the people as a whole; the adjective inside public house.
entries.definitionCN: 向所有人开放的，或指全体民众；public house 里用的正是这个形容词。

entries.definition: To make a text available to the public; built on the same Latin family as public.
entries.definitionCN: 使文字向公众发行；与 public 同出一个拉丁词族。

entries.definition: A counter or room where drinks are served and drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 供应并供人饮用酒水的柜台或房间。

entries.definition: An old word for a place that sells drink and often food.
entries.definitionCN: 指卖酒、常兼供食物的旧词。

entries.definition: A small hotel that also serves meals and drink.
entries.definitionCN: 兼供饭食与酒水的小旅店。

entries.definition: A bar, especially in the old American West.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指美国旧西部的酒吧。

normalIntro.en: The word is a three-word phrase squeezed into one syllable, and behind that phrase stands a Latin adjective for what belongs to the people.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个三词短语压成了一个音节，而短语背后是一个表示「属于人民」的拉丁形容词。

normal.en: Pub is public house cut short: the endings fall away and two words become one syllable.
normal.cn: pub 是 public house 的截短：词尾脱落，两个词压缩成一个音节。

normal.en: The public in public house is Latin publicus, from populus, the people, so a pub was a house open to the people.
normal.cn: public house 里的 public 来自拉丁 publicus，而 publicus 出自 populus（人民），所以 pub 原本就是对人民开放的房子。

normal.en: A publican runs the pub, although the same Latin word once meant a tax collector, a very different trade.
normal.cn: publican 是经营酒馆的人，尽管同一个拉丁词从前指收税的人，两者行当大不相同。

normal.en: Pub quiz and pub lunch keep pub in front of a noun, marking something that happens inside that place.
normal.cn: pub quiz 与 pub lunch 把 pub 放在名词前，标明那件事就发生在这个场所里。

normal.en: In Australia and New Zealand one word covers the bar and the bedrooms, because one building once did both jobs.
normal.cn: 在澳大利亚与新西兰，一个词同时覆盖酒吧与客房，因为从前一栋房子就兼做这两件事。

abstract.en: The word is a door swinging open on a warm evening, with strangers sitting close enough to talk.
abstract.cn: 这个词就是一扇在暖夜里推开的门，里面的陌生人坐得近到可以交谈。

abstract.en: Cutting a long phrase down to one beat is how a language makes room for the thing people do most often.
abstract.cn: 把一个长短语砍成一个节拍，是语言在为人们最常做的事腾出位置。

abstract.en: A pub sells drink, but people come back for the same three chairs and the same familiar noise.
abstract.cn: 酒馆卖的是酒，可人们回来找的是同样那三把椅子和同样熟悉的喧闹。

examples.en: We had lunch at a pub by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边一家酒馆吃了午饭。

examples.en: The pub closes at eleven on weekdays.
examples.cn: 这家酒馆工作日十一点关门。

examples.en: He now runs the pub his grandfather opened.
examples.cn: 他现在经营着祖父当年开的那家酒馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「帕布」——推门进去，帕布一声放下杯子，就是街角那家酒馆。

root: pub 是英语短语 public house（向公众开放的房子）在十九世纪的截短形式；public 出自拉丁语 publicus，publicus 又来自 populus（人民）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a house open to the public for drink; the senses divide into the British drinking room, the Australian hotel, the role of neighbourhood centre, and the attributive use before another noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「向公众开放、可供饮酒的房子」；义项由此分出英式饮酒场所、澳新旅店、街坊聚点的角色，以及放在名词前的定语用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corner doorway with a warm lamp above it, swinging open on a room full of talk.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角一扇挂着暖灯的门，被推开，里面满是说话声。

branches.en: a warm doorway on a wet evening
branches.cn: 雨夜里透出暖光的一扇门

branches.en: the same three chairs filled every night
branches.cn: 每晚都坐满的同样三把椅子

branches.en: a highway inn with rooms above the bar
branches.cn: 公路旁楼上带客房的旅店

branches.en: a chalkboard listing Sunday lunches
branches.cn: 写着周日午餐的小黑板

branches.en: one word for a room and for a habit
branches.cn: 一个词既指一间屋子，也指一种习惯

intro.en: The word is held together by the Latin noun for the people, the adjective built on it, the English phrase public house, and the clipped form pub.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示人民的拉丁名词、由它构成的形容词、英语短语 public house，以及截短形式 pub 共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 宗教；宗教信仰；执着的追求
definition_en: belief in a god or gods, and the system of worship and moral rules that goes with it
core_image: 一条把人反复系回神圣之物的绳索
scene: 每天做早饭之前，外婆都会在小神龛前点香、合掌。 Every morning before cooking, my grandmother practices her religion at the small altar.
sceneCN: 这里 religion 是「宗教」（第 2 个义项：一套信仰与仪式体系）；句意：每天做饭前，外婆都会在小神龛前进行她的宗教活动。

pos.zh: 宗教；宗教信仰；执着的追求

derivatives.zh: religion 加 -ous 构成，义为「宗教的；虔诚的」
religious 加 -ly 构成，义为「虔诚地；一丝不苟地」

senses.title: Belief in a divine power
senses.definition: the belief that a god or gods exist and that people should worship them
senses.definitionCN: 相信存在神并应当对其崇拜的信念
senses.example: Religion gave the villagers comfort after the earthquake.
senses.exampleCN: 地震之后，宗教信仰给了村民们安慰。
senses.why: If the old root means to bind, then religion is the cord that ties a person to the divine.
senses.whyCN: 如果古老的词根意为「系紧」，那么宗教就是把人与神明系在一起的那根绳索。

senses.title: A system of faith and worship
senses.definition: one of the organized systems of faith, ritual, and moral teaching followed by a group
senses.definitionCN: 一群人遵循的、由信仰、仪式与道德教义组成的有组织体系
senses.example: Buddhism is one of the great religions of Asia.
senses.exampleCN: 佛教是亚洲的伟大宗教之一。
senses.why: A single binding cord becomes a shared framework when a whole community is tied by the same beliefs and rites.
senses.whyCN: 当整个群体被同一套信仰与仪式系在一起，那一根绳索就变成了一套共同体系。

senses.title: Something pursued with devotion
senses.definition: an activity that someone treats with the seriousness and devotion normally given to a faith
senses.definitionCN: 某人以近乎信仰的认真与投入对待的活动
senses.example: For him, fitness is a religion rather than a hobby.
senses.exampleCN: 对他而言，健身不是爱好，而是一种信仰。
senses.why: The binding force of faith can be transferred to any practice that rules a person's days, hence the figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 信仰那种系住人的力量可以转移到任何支配日常生活的活动上，于是有了这个比喻用法。

intro.en: The origin of religion is debated. Most reference works point to Latin religare, to bind fast, while others argue for relegere, to read over again.
intro.cn: religion 的词源存在争议：多数辞书认为来自拉丁语 religare「系紧」，也有学者主张来自 relegere「反复阅读、重新重视」。

items.en: Religare combines re- with ligare, to bind, and means to tie fast.
items.cn: religare 由 re- 与 ligare「捆绑」组合，意为牢牢系住。

items.en: Relegere means to read over again or to go over carefully, and is the rival explanation.
items.cn: relegere 意为反复阅读或仔细重温，是另一种解释的来源。

items.en: Religio in classical Latin covers scruple, reverence, and the fear of the gods.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语 religio 涵盖顾忌、敬畏以及对神明的畏惧。

items.en: Old French religion names a monastic order as well as a system of faith.
items.cn: 古法语 religion 既指修会，也指信仰体系。

items.en: English adopts religion for a system of faith and for the state of being devout.
items.cn: 英语在十三世纪引入 religion，指信仰体系与虔诚的状态。

items.en: The modern word keeps the system sense and adds the playful sense of a devoted pursuit.
items.cn: 现代英语保留「体系」之义，并增添了「执着追求」这一戏谑用法。

note.en: Religion sits beside words for belief, and it looks like several Latin words built on the same re- prefix.
note.cn: religion 与表示「信念」的词相邻，外形上也与若干由 re- 开头的拉丁词相近。

entries.definition: relating to religion or believing strongly in it
entries.definitionCN: 宗教的；虔诚的，由 religion 加 -ous 构成

entries.definition: in a very regular and careful way
entries.definitionCN: 一丝不苟地；虔诚地

entries.definition: to bind together, a rare technical verb
entries.definitionCN: 捆扎；系紧，是罕见的技术用词，与 religion 共享 ligare 词根

entries.definition: strong belief in a religion or in someone
entries.definitionCN: 信仰；信任，侧重内心的确信

entries.definition: a feeling that something is true or real
entries.definitionCN: 信念；看法，范围比 religion 更宽

entries.definition: a formal statement of religious belief
entries.definitionCN: 信条；教义，是宗教信念的正式表述

normalIntro.en: The word is usually explained through Latin ligare, to bind, so most hooks use the image of a tie.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词通常用拉丁语 ligare「捆绑」来解释，所以记忆钩子多用「系住」的画面。

normal.en: Religion and ligament share the lig- root of binding; one ties a person to a faith.
normal.cn: religion 与 ligament 共享表示「捆绑」的 lig- 词根，一个系住人，一个系住骨。

normal.en: The adjective religious adds -ous, and the adverb religiously adds -ly after that.
normal.cn: 形容词 religious 加了 -ous，副词 religiously 再在其后加 -ly。

normal.en: Religiously also means doing something very regularly, as if it were a ritual.
normal.cn: religiously 还表示极为规律地做某事，像是在行仪式。

normal.en: Freedom of religion is a fixed phrase worth learning as one block.
normal.cn: freedom of religion 是值得整块记住的固定表达。

normal.en: Remember that the binding explanation is the usual one but not the only hypothesis.
normal.cn: 记住「捆绑」是通行解释，但并非唯一假说。

abstract.en: Picture a rope looped around a person and tied to a high stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子绕过一个人，系在高处的石头上。

abstract.en: See a whole village kneeling in the same direction at dawn.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时整个村庄朝同一个方向跪拜。

abstract.en: Think of a runner who treats a morning run like a sacred duty.
abstract.cn: 想一位把晨跑当成神圣义务的跑者。

examples.en: Religion has shaped the art and music of this region.
examples.cn: 宗教塑造了这个地区的艺术与音乐。

examples.en: The law protects freedom of religion for every citizen.
examples.cn: 法律保护每位公民的宗教信仰自由。

examples.en: He follows his religion with great care.
examples.cn: 他非常认真地奉行自己的宗教。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞丽珍」——想象把珍视的信念系在身上；只是谐音联想，与真实词源无关。

root: 一般认为来自拉丁语 religare（re-「牢牢地」+ ligare「捆绑」），另有 relegere（反复阅读）一说，词源存争议。

sensesIntro.en: From one binding cord come the personal belief, the organized system, and the devotion given to anything at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一根系紧的绳索，长出个人的信仰、有组织的体系，以及对任何事物的执着投入。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope tying a person back to something sacred.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条把人与神圣之物系在一起的绳索。

branches.en: The tie is felt first as personal belief.
branches.cn: 这根绳索最先被感受为个人的信仰。

branches.en: When a community shares the tie, it becomes an organized system.
branches.cn: 当整个群体共享这根绳索，它就成为有组织的体系。

branches.en: The same binding force can grip a hobby, giving the figurative sense.
branches.cn: 同样的系缚之力也能抓住一项爱好，产生比喻义。

branches.en: Personal belief and shared system are two scales of the same bond.
branches.cn: 个人信仰与共同体系是同一种纽带的两个尺度。

branches.en: Both a church and a cherished routine rule the order of a day.
branches.cn: 教会与珍视的日常习惯都支配着一天的秩序。

intro.en: Religion is a Latin noun with a prefix, a root, and a suffix, all carried into English through French.
intro.cn: religion 是一个拉丁名词，含前缀、词根与词尾，经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- strengthens the action, ligare means to bind, and -io names the resulting state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 加强动作，ligare 表示「捆绑」，词尾 -io 表示由此形成的状态。

items.example: Re- tightens the action in religare.
items.exampleCN: 在 religare 中，前缀 re- 加强了动作。

items.example: The lig- root also binds in ligament.
items.exampleCN: lig- 词根在 ligament 中也表示系缚。

items.example: Ligare is the verb behind the lig- root.
items.exampleCN: ligare 是 lig- 词根背后的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -io turns the verb into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -io 把动词变成表示状态的名词。

items.example: Religare is the usual source given for religion.
items.exampleCN: religare 是 religion 通常被追溯到的来源。

items.example: Religio already carries both fear and worship.
items.exampleCN: religio 同时带有畏惧与崇拜两层意思。

items.meaning: a band of tissue that ties bones together
items.example: Ligament keeps the binding sense of ligare.
items.exampleCN: ligament 保留了 ligare 的「系缚」含义。

items.meaning: a duty that ties a person to an action
items.example: Obligation adds ob- to the same ligare root.
items.exampleCN: obligation 在同一个 ligare 词根前加了 ob-。

definition_zh: 潜在的；可能的；有潜力的；（名词）潜力；电势；势能
definition_en: possible but not yet actual; having the capacity to develop into something; (noun) the capacity to become something in the future
core_image: 一枚还没拉开的弓：力已经存着，只是尚未射出
scene: 药房里，药剂师指着说明书上的警示行。 She said: Potential side effects make this drug dangerous when it is taken with alcohol.
sceneCN: 这里 potential 是「潜在的、可能发生但还没发生的」（第 1 个义项：以一种可能性的方式存在）；句意：潜在的副作用会让这种药与酒精同服时变得危险。场景要点：还没发生、但条件一凑就会发生；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 潜在的；可能的；有潜力的

derivatives.zh: 强有力的；有效的（同出 posse）
全能的（omni- 全部 + potens 有能力）

senses.title: Possible but not yet actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在的：可能发生，但还没发生
senses.definition: existing as a possibility rather than as a fact
senses.definitionCN: 以一种可能性的方式存在，而非作为事实存在
senses.example: The drug is potentially dangerous if taken with alcohol.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药如果与酒精同服，可能有危险。
senses.why: Latin posse means 'to be able'. Potential marks what is able to happen without having happened yet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 posse 意为“能够”。potential 标记的是“能够发生、但尚未发生”的东西。

senses.title: Having latent ability
senses.titleCN: 有潜力的：本事藏着，还没使出来
senses.definition: having an ability that is not yet developed or shown
senses.definitionCN: 拥有尚未发展或尚未显现的能力
senses.example: She is a potential national champion in the 800 metres.
senses.exampleCN: 她有可能成为 800 米全国冠军。
senses.why: The same 'able to be' applies to a person: the capacity is real, the achievement is not yet.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“能够成为”用在人身上：能力是真实的，成就还没到。

senses.title: Physics: stored energy
senses.titleCN: 势能：存着还没放出来的能量
senses.definition: energy that a body has because of its position or condition, rather than because of motion
senses.definitionCN: 物体因位置或状态而具有的能量，而非因运动而具有的能量
senses.example: The water behind the dam has a great deal of potential energy.
senses.exampleCN: 坝后的水具有大量势能。
senses.why: Energy held in place is ability waiting to be released. Physics named it with the same word for capacity.
senses.whyCN: 被位置存住的能量，就是等着被释放的“能够”。物理学用了同一个表示“能力”的词来命名它。

senses.title: Physics: electric potential
senses.titleCN: 电势：电场里某点的“位势”
senses.definition: the amount of electric potential energy per unit charge at a point in a field
senses.definitionCN: 电场中某点单位电荷所具有的电势能
senses.example: Current flows from higher to lower electric potential.
senses.exampleCN: 电流从电势较高处流向电势较低处。
senses.why: A charge at a point in a field has stored ability to move. That stored ability, measured per charge, is the potential.
senses.whyCN: 电场中某点的电荷存有移动的能力。把这份储存的能力按单位电荷计量，就是电势。

senses.title: Grammar: expressing possibility
senses.titleCN: 语法：表示可能性的语气
senses.definition: in grammar, describing a mood or form that presents something as possible rather than real
senses.definitionCN: 语法上指把某事呈现为可能而非现实的形式或语气
senses.example: In some languages the potential mood marks what may happen.
senses.exampleCN: 有些语言用可能语气标记可能发生的事。
senses.why: Grammar borrows the word to name the form whose job is exactly this: stating what can be, without stating that it is.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用这个词，来命名那种专门做这件事的形式：说出“可能是什么”，而不说“就是什么”。

senses.title: Noun: the possibility of something
senses.titleCN: 名词：某事发生的可能性
senses.definition: the possibility that something will happen or can be developed
senses.definitionCN: 某事将会发生或可以被发展出来的可能性
senses.example: The potential for conflict remains high in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区发生冲突的可能性仍然很高。
senses.why: The adjective's abstract quality becomes a noun: not a possible thing, but possibility itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词的抽象性质变成名词：不是某个可能之物，而是“可能性”本身。

senses.title: Noun: undeveloped capacity in a person
senses.titleCN: 名词：一个人身上尚未长成的本事
senses.definition: the capacity a person has to develop and succeed in the future
senses.definitionCN: 一个人在未来发展与取得成就的能力
senses.example: The coach saw potential in the young goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在这个年轻守门员身上看到了潜力。
senses.why: A person is treated like a body with stored energy: what is there now is less than what it can become.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成一个储能的身体：现在已有的，少于它将来能成为的。

senses.title: Physics: potential difference
senses.titleCN: 电势差：两点之间的位势落差
senses.definition: the difference in electric potential between two points, measured in volts
senses.definitionCN: 两点之间电势的差值，以伏特计
senses.example: A battery maintains a potential difference across its terminals.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在其两端维持一个电势差。
senses.why: Difference is what makes stored ability flow. The gap between two potentials is the push that moves charge.
senses.whyCN: 落差才使储存的能力流动。两个电势之间的差距，就是推动电荷移动的那股力。

intro.en: Potential comes from the Latin verb for being able. The idea is capacity that has not yet turned into act, which is why the word serves both for people and for stored energy.
intro.cn: potential 来自拉丁语中表示“能够”的动词。其观念是“尚未变成现实的能力”，所以它既可用于人，也可用于储存的能量。

items.en: Posse meant 'to be able, to have power'. It is a compound of potis 'able' plus esse 'to be', literally 'to be able'.
items.cn: posse 意为“能够、有力量”。它由 potis“有能力的”加 esse“存在、是”构成，字面即“能够是”。

items.en: The present participle potens meant 'being able, powerful'. English potent and omnipotent come from this form.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens 意为“有能力的、强大的”。英语 potent 与 omnipotent 来自这个形式。

items.en: Potentia meant 'power, ability, capacity'. It names the quality rather than the act, which is exactly the seed of the modern word.
items.cn: potentia 意为“力量、能力、潜能”。它命名的是性质而非行动，这正是现代这个词的种子。

items.en: Potentialis was formed from potentia plus -alis, meaning 'having power or capacity'. Medieval philosophy used it for what can exist without existing yet.
items.cn: potentialis 由 potentia 加 -alis 构成，意为“具有力量或能力的”。中世纪哲学用它指“能够存在但尚未存在”的东西。

items.en: English potential enters in the 17th century, first in philosophy and grammar. The scientific senses of potential energy and electric potential follow in the 19th century.
items.cn: 英语 potential 于 17 世纪进入，最早用于哲学与语法。势能与电势的科学义则在 19 世纪跟进。

items.en: Modern English uses it for latent ability in people, for possible risks and customers, and for the technical quantities named after stored energy.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指人身上尚未显现的能力、可能的风险与客户，以及那些以储存能量命名的技术量。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root for being able. The second group collects words for what may happen and what is not yet developed.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“能够”的词根。第二组收表示“可能发生”与“尚未发展”的词。

entries.definition: possibly, in a way that may become real. It softens a claim: potentially dangerous means may be dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 可能地，以某种或将成真的方式。它使断言变软：potentially dangerous 意为“可能有危险”。

entries.definition: powerful or effective. Potent describes power already present; potential describes power not yet used.
entries.definitionCN: 强有力的、有效的。potent 描述已经在场的力；potential 描述尚未使用的力。

entries.definition: the state of being possible or having latent capacity. It is the philosophical noun built on potential.
entries.definitionCN: 处于可能状态或具有潜在能力。它是建立在 potential 之上的哲学名词。

entries.definition: all-powerful. Omni- 'all' plus potens 'able': able to do everything.
entries.definitionCN: 全能的。omni-“全部”加 potens“有能力的”：能做一切。

entries.definition: able to happen or be true. Possible is wider; potential often suggests a capacity that can be developed.
entries.definitionCN: 能够发生或为真。possible 更宽；potential 常暗示一种可以被发展出来的能力。

entries.definition: present but not yet active or visible. Latent stresses hiddenness; potential stresses capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未活动或显现。latent 强调隐藏；potential 强调能力。

entries.definition: likely to happen or to become something in the future. Prospective is about the future position; potential is about the capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 未来可能发生或成为的。prospective 关乎未来的位置；potential 关乎能力。

entries.definition: signs that someone or something will do well. Promise is the informal judgement; potential is the neutral capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 表明某人或某物会出色的迹象。promise 是非正式的判断；potential 是中性的能力。

entries.definition: the amount something can hold or do. Capacity is measurable; potential can be unmeasured and unrealized.
entries.definitionCN: 某物能容纳或能做到的量。capacity 可测量；potential 可以未被测量、未被实现。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the drawn bow, the unseen champion, the water behind the dam, the battery terminal, and the coach's eye.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：拉开的弓、还没出头的冠军、坝后的水、电池两端、教练的眼光。

normal.en: Potential is a drawn bow: the force is already stored, only the release has not happened.
normal.cn: potential 是一张拉开的弓：力已经存好，只是还没放箭。

normal.en: A potential champion is someone whose trophy is still in the future.
normal.cn: a potential champion 是奖杯还在未来的人。

normal.en: Water held behind a dam is potential energy: high up, still, waiting.
normal.cn: 坝后存住的水就是势能：位置高、静止、等着。

normal.en: A battery keeps a potential difference: one terminal is higher than the other, and charge wants to flow down.
normal.cn: 电池维持电势差：一端比另一端高，电荷就想往下流。

normal.en: A coach sees potential, which means seeing the future player inside the present one.
normal.cn: 教练看到潜力，就是从现在这个球员身上看到未来的那个。

abstract.en: Potential is the gap between what is and what could be, and every measurement of it is a guess about the future.
abstract.cn: 潜力是“是什么”与“可能是什么”之间的落差，对它的每一次测量都是对未来的猜测。

abstract.en: Stored energy and undeveloped talent share one word because both are ability held in place.
abstract.cn: 储存的能量与未发展的才能共用一个词，因为两者都是被位置存住的“能够”。

abstract.en: Calling something potential is a way of praising it without yet committing to it.
abstract.cn: 称某物为 potential，是一种既赞美它、又尚未对它作出承诺的说法。

examples.en: The region has enormous potential for solar power.
examples.cn: 该地区在太阳能方面有巨大潜力。

examples.en: Investors were warned about the potential loss of their deposits.
examples.cn: 投资者被警告存款可能遭受损失。

examples.en: She never reached her full potential as a runner because of injuries.
examples.cn: 因为伤病，她从未跑出自己全部的潜力。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破天秀”——还没出手就已经很秀，潜力（potential）藏在天分里

root: 拉丁语 posse“能够”（potis“有能力的”+ esse“是”）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“能力”→ 晚期拉丁 potentialis → 英语 potential（17 世纪）。

sensesIntro.en: Everything turns on the difference between able-to-be and being. A possible event, an undeveloped talent, stored energy, a voltage, and a grammatical mood all describe capacity before it becomes act.
sensesIntro.cn: 一切都围绕“能够成为”与“已经成为”的差别。可能发生的事、未发展的才能、储存的能量、电压、语法语气，描述的都是“变成行动之前的能力”。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched bow held still, force stored and not yet released.
core.cn: 核心意象：拉满却静持的弓，力已储存，尚未放出。

branches.en: POSSIBILITY: what may happen, stated as an adjective and as a noun.
branches.cn: 可能性：可能发生之事，分别用形容词与名词表达。

branches.en: TALENT: capacity inside a person, seen by a coach or by the person herself.
branches.cn: 才能：人身上的能力，被教练或本人看见。

branches.en: STORED ENERGY: the bow, the dam, the lifted weight.
branches.cn: 储能：弓、坝、被举高的重物。

branches.en: ELECTRICITY: the level at a point and the difference between two points.
branches.cn: 电学：某点的电势与两点之间的电势差。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: the form whose whole job is to say 'may be'.
branches.cn: 语法：专门负责说“可能是”的那个形式。

intro.en: The family is built on the Latin verb for being able. Its participles and abstract nouns supply potent, potential, and potentiality; prefixes add scope such as all or many.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在拉丁语表示“能够”的动词上。它的分词与抽象名词提供了 potent、potential、potentiality；前缀则加上“全部”“多”等范围。

latinIntro.en: Latin potens and potentia passed into English through scientific and philosophical writing, so the technical senses retain their Latin shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potens 与 potentia 经科学与哲学写作进入英语，所以技术义仍保留拉丁形态。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 多能的（能分化成多种细胞）

definition_zh: 牢靠的；安心的；获得；使牢固
definition_en: fixed or fastened so that it cannot be lost or opened easily; free from worry; to get or make firm
core_image: 一把扣紧的锁，门被牢牢固定，里面的人不再担心
scene: 银行新装的门锁经过测试，工作人员确认一切稳妥。 The new vault door is secure, so nobody can break in at night.
sceneCN: 这里 secure 是「牢固的、锁紧的」（第 1 个义项：固定不动、不易被打开）；句意是新金库门很牢固，夜里没人能闯进来。

derivatives.zh: 由 secure 加 -ity 名词后缀构成，义为「安全；保障」
secure 加 -ly 副词后缀，义为「牢固地；安心地」
加否定前缀 in-，义为「不安全的；不自信的」

senses.title: Fastened or locked firmly
senses.definition: made firm so that it cannot move, fall, or be opened easily
senses.definitionCN: 固定得很紧，不会移动、掉落或轻易被打开
senses.example: Make sure the rope is secure before you climb.
senses.exampleCN: 爬之前要确认绳子已经系牢。
senses.why: The core image is a locked door: something has been physically fastened so it stays in place.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是扣紧的门：某物被固定住，稳稳待在原位。

senses.title: Free from danger or worry
senses.definition: safe from harm, and not worried about losing something
senses.definitionCN: 不受伤害的威胁，也不担心失去什么
senses.example: With a steady income she finally felt secure.
senses.exampleCN: 有了稳定收入，她终于感到安心。
senses.why: When the door is locked, the person inside stops worrying — physical firmness becomes emotional safety.
senses.whyCN: 门锁好了，里面的人不再担心——物理上的牢固引申为内心的安稳。

senses.title: To obtain something after effort
senses.definition: to get something that you want, especially after trying hard
senses.definitionCN: 经过努力得到想要的东西，尤指来之不易之物
senses.example: She secured a scholarship after months of practice.
senses.exampleCN: 经过几个月练习，她拿到了奖学金。
senses.why: Locking something in means you finally hold it — gaining it and keeping it at once.
senses.whyCN: 「锁住」意味着你终于握住了它——得到并留住。

senses.title: To fasten or hold firmly
senses.definition: to attach or fix something firmly in place
senses.definitionCN: 把某物牢牢固定或连接在某个位置
senses.example: The crew secured the cargo before the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 船员在风暴来临前把货物固定好。
senses.why: The same image of the locked door works as an action: you are the one who fastens it.
senses.whyCN: 还是那扇扣紧的门，这次变成动作：由你来把它固定住。

senses.title: Protected from loss or risk
senses.definition: protected so that money, information, or rights cannot be taken away
senses.definitionCN: 受到保护，钱财、信息或权利不会被夺走
senses.example: Please keep your documents in a secure place.
senses.exampleCN: 请把文件放在有保障的地方。
senses.why: A locked vault protects what is inside, so the word extends to anything guarded.
senses.whyCN: 上了锁的保险库保护里面的东西，这个词便延伸到一切被守护的对象。

intro.en: From Latin securus, meaning free from care, built on se- (free from) and cura (care).
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 securus，意为「无忧虑的」，由 se-（免除）与 cura（操心）构成。

items.en: The root *kweye- means to pay attention or care; it also gives Latin cura.
items.cn: 重构词根 *kweye- 表示「留意、操心」，也派生出拉丁语 cura。

items.en: Securus combines se- (apart, free from) with cura (care), so it literally means free from care.
items.cn: 拉丁语 securus 由 se-（脱离）加 cura（操心）构成，字面义是「免于操心」。

items.en: The word passed into Old French as seur, meaning safe and certain.
items.cn: 该词进入古法语作 seur，意为「安全的、确定的」。

items.en: Middle French forms such as seur and secure influenced English borrowing.
items.cn: 中世纪法语形式 seur、secure 影响了英语的借用。

items.en: English took secure in the 1500s, first meaning free from fear, then fixed firmly.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 secure，先表「不再恐惧」，后表「固定牢靠」。

items.en: Today it covers firm attachment, safety, confidence, and obtaining something.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖牢固、安全、安心以及获得等含义。

note.en: Words that look or sound like secure, and near-meaning rivals in the field of safety.
note.cn: 与 secure 拼写相近的词，以及安全义场中的近义对手。

entries.definition: to keep someone apart from other people
entries.definitionCN: 使隔绝；使隐退——拼写与 secure 相近，但词义完全不同，无同源关系

entries.definition: eager to know or learn something
entries.definitionCN: 好奇的——与 secure 共享拉丁 cura 的远源联想易混淆，词形并不相同，注意区分

entries.definition: certain and without doubt
entries.definitionCN: 确定的——与 secure 同源于拉丁 securus 经法语的简化形式

entries.definition: out of danger and not harmed
entries.definitionCN: 安全的——强调处境无危险，secure 更强调固定与保障

entries.definition: to close or fix something firmly
entries.definitionCN: 系紧；固定——与 secure 的动词义相近，但不含获得义

entries.definition: to get something you want
entries.definitionCN: 取得——与 secure 的「获得」义项近义，但 secure 更强调保住成果

normalIntro.en: Memory hooks built on the real root cura (care) and the locked-door image.
normalIntro.cn: 基于真实词根 cura（操心）与锁门画面的记忆钩子。

normal.en: se- means free from + cura means care, so secure is free from care
normal.cn: se- 表示「免除」+ cura 表示「操心」，secure 字面就是「免于操心」

normal.en: sure and secure share the same Old French ancestor
normal.cn: sure 与 secure 同出一脉，都来自古法语

normal.en: the locked vault is the core picture of the adjective
normal.cn: 上了锁的金库就是形容词义的核心画面

normal.en: secure a job = lock the job in so you cannot lose it
normal.cn: secure a job 就是把工作「锁进保险柜」，不会丢

normal.en: in- reverses it: insecure means not safe and not confident
normal.cn: 加上 in- 就反转：insecure 既不安全也不自信

abstract.en: Picture clicking a padlock shut and feeling your shoulders relax
abstract.cn: 想象咔哒一声扣上挂锁，肩膀随之放松的画面

abstract.en: See a rope tied with a double knot that nothing can shake
abstract.cn: 看见一根绳打了双结，怎么晃都不会松

abstract.en: Feel the moment your offer letter arrives and the worry drains away
abstract.cn: 体会录取通知到达那一刻，担忧一扫而空的感受

examples.en: The engineer secured the ladder before painting the wall.
examples.cn: 油漆工先把梯子固定好再刷墙。

examples.en: She finally secured a contract with the city government.
examples.cn: 她终于和市政府签下了合同。

examples.en: A secure network keeps hackers out of the system.
examples.cn: 安全的网络把黑客挡在系统之外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「色库了」——东西锁进色库（仓库）里了，牢牢的，谁也拿不走，所以又牢固又安心。

root: 拉丁语 se-（免除）+ cura（操心、照料，与 curious 同出一源）构成 securus「免于操心的」；经古法语 seur 进入英语。secure 的「固定」「安心」「获得」三义都从「锁住无忧」生长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From the locked vault picture, the word fans out into firmness, safety, and gain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「上锁的金库」这一画面出发，词义展开为牢固、安全与获得。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a locked vault — firmly shut and worry-free
core.cn: 核心意象：上了锁的金库——关得牢牢的，不再操心

branches.en: firm attachment and the act of fixing things down
branches.cn: 物理上的系紧与固定动作

branches.en: inner calm once danger is out of reach
branches.cn: 危险被挡在外面后的内心安稳

branches.en: winning and keeping something valuable
branches.cn: 赢得并守住有价值的东西

branches.en: the door stays shut and the mind stays quiet
branches.cn: 门关得住，心也静得下来

branches.en: you are the one turning the key
branches.cn: 你正是转钥匙的那个人

intro.en: English words built around the Latin pair se- (free from) and cura (care).
intro.cn: 围绕拉丁语 se-（免除）与 cura（操心）构成的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin relatives that share the cura root.
latinIntro.cn: 共享 cura 词根的拉丁同族词。

items.exampleCN: 陪审团被隔离，与外界分开。

items.example: Curation means taking care of a collection.
items.exampleCN: 「策展」就是悉心照料一批藏品。

items.example: Secure the window before the typhoon.
items.exampleCN: 台风来之前把窗户固定好。

He felt insecure about his new role.

items.exampleCN: 机场安检检查每一件行李。

items.meaning: to take care of and select content
items.example: She curates the gallery each spring.
items.exampleCN: 她每年春天为画廊策展。

items.meaningCN: 模糊的；晦涩的——与 secure 形近但词源不同，来自拉丁 ob- 加基词 cuvere
items.example: The meaning of the poem remains obscure.
items.exampleCN: 这首诗的含义仍不明朗。

definition_zh: 最大值；最大量；上限；最大的；最高的；（数学）极大值
definition_en: the greatest amount, size, or level that is possible, allowed, or recorded, also used before a noun for the greatest of its kind
core_image: 一根标尺顶到最后一格，指针再也推不上去
scene: 测试台上，工程师把发动机转速一点点推高，仪表的指针最后停在再往上就会报警的那一格。 The engine was running at maximum speed when the warning light came on.
sceneCN: 这里 maximum 是「最大值、上限」（第 1 个义项：可以达到的最大量）；句意为报警灯亮起时，发动机正以最高转速运转。图中可辨识物件：测试台、仪表盘、红色指针。

pos.zh: 最大值；最大量；上限；极大值
最大的；最高的；最大限度的

derivatives.zh: 由 maximum 的词干 max- 加 -al 构成，义为「最大的；达到极限的」
由 max- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使最大化」
由 maximize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「最大化」
由 maximal 加 -ly 构成，义为「最大限度地」

senses.title: The greatest amount or level allowed
senses.definition: the greatest amount, size, or level that is possible, allowed, or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 可能达到、被允许或记录到的最大数量、规模或水平
senses.example: The tank holds a maximum of fifty litres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个油箱最多装五十升。
senses.why: Latin maximus already means greatest, so the noun names the top value of a scale rather than a thing you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maximus 本义就是「最大的」，所以这个名词直接指刻度上的顶端数值，而不是能够摸到的实物。

senses.title: The greatest of its kind
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe the greatest size, speed, or level that is allowed or reached
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，描述被允许或达到的最大规模、速度或水平
senses.example: The car's maximum load is printed on the door.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的最大载重印在车门上。
senses.why: Because maximus is a superlative, the word can stand before a noun and mark that noun as the top of its scale.
senses.whyCN: 因为 maximus 是最高级形式，这个词便能放在名词前，把这个名词标在它那一量级的顶端。

senses.title: The highest point reached in a process
senses.definition: the highest point that a changing quantity reaches before it falls again
senses.definitionCN: 一个变化的量在回落之前所达到的最高点
senses.example: Demand for water reaches its maximum in midsummer.
senses.exampleCN: 对水的需求在盛夏达到峰值。
senses.why: Once the top value has a name, it can also name the moment a curve turns over, so the word moves from a limit to a peak in time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦顶端数值有了名字，它也能指曲线转向的那一刻，于是词义从「界限」转到时间上的「峰值」。

senses.title: The largest value of a mathematical function
senses.definition: the largest value of a function, either in a small neighbourhood or over its whole range
senses.definitionCN: 函数在某一小范围内或整个取值范围内的最大取值
senses.example: The curve shows a maximum near the middle of the graph.
senses.exampleCN: 曲线在图的中间附近出现一个极大值。
senses.why: Mathematicians kept the Latin word because a function's top value is literally the greatest number the formula can produce.
senses.whyCN: 数学家保留了这个拉丁词，因为函数的最大取值字面上就是公式能算出的最大数值。

intro.en: Maximum is a Latin superlative borrowed whole into English, so its history is the story of the word for great rising to its highest degree.
intro.cn: maximum 是把拉丁语最高级原样借进英语的词，它的历史就是「大」这个词一步步升到最高程度的故事。

items.en: Magnus meant great or large, and it is the positive degree behind a whole family of size words.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的、伟大的」，是整族表示大小的词的原级。

items.en: Maximus was the superlative of magnus, literally the greatest, used of persons as well as things.
items.cn: maximus 是 magnus 的最高级，字面就是「最大的」，也曾用来形容人。

items.en: The neuter form maximum named the greatest amount as a thing in itself, a pattern common in Latin technical writing.
items.cn: 中性形式 maximum 把「最大的量」当作独立的东西来指称，这在拉丁学术写作中很常见。

items.en: English took maximum as a learned word of mathematics and natural philosophy, usually paired with minimum.
items.cn: 英语在十七至十八世纪把 maximum 作为数学与自然哲学的学术词引入，通常与 minimum 配对。

items.en: Modern English uses it as both noun and adjective, from engine speed to legal sentences and everyday caps.
items.cn: 现代英语把它同时用作名词和形容词，从发动机转速到法律刑期再到日常上限都用它。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family of magnus and maximus; the near-meaning group gathers words for the top of a scale.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 magnus 与 maximus 的拉丁词族走；近义组收表示刻度顶端的词。

entries.definition: As great as possible; the adjective built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能大的；由同一词干构成的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something as great as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能大；最大化。

entries.definition: The Latin superlative meaning greatest, the direct source of maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语最高级，意为「最大的」，是 maximum 的直接来源。

entries.definition: Size or extent, especially of something large.
entries.definitionCN: 大小；量级，尤指大的事物的规模。

entries.definition: The smallest amount or level that is possible or allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 可能或被允许的最小数量或水平；最小值。

entries.definition: The highest point of a process or period.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或时期中的最高点；峰值。

entries.definition: The upper limit set on an amount or rate.
entries.definitionCN: 为数量或比率设定的上限。

entries.definition: The greatest possible degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物可能达到的最大程度。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin superlative, so every memory route leads back to a scale with a top rung.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一个拉丁语最高级，所以每条记忆线索都回到「有一格的刻度」这个意象。

normal.en: Maximus is the superlative of magnus, so maximum is literally the greatest degree of great.
normal.cn: maximus 是 magnus 的最高级，所以 maximum 字面上就是「大」的最高程度。

normal.en: The ending -imum is the Latin neuter, which is why maximum can act as a noun for the greatest amount.
normal.cn: 词尾 -imum 是拉丁语中性形式，所以 maximum 能当名词，指最大的量。

normal.en: Maximal, maximize and maximally all keep the max- stem: the top of the scale as adjective, verb and adverb.
normal.cn: maximal、maximize、maximally 都保留 max- 词干，分别把「顶端」做成形容词、动词和副词。

normal.en: Maximum pairs with minimum in technical writing, the two ends of one measuring scale.
normal.cn: maximum 在学术写作里与 minimum 配对，是同一条量尺的两端。

normal.en: A maximum sentence is the longest term a court may impose, which is the same top-of-scale idea in law.
normal.cn: maximum sentence 是法院能判的最长刑期，法律里用的仍是同一个「刻度顶端」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose last mark is painted red: that mark is the maximum.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，最后一格被涂成红色，那一格就是最大值。

abstract.en: A thermometer stops rising at noon and then falls; that stopping point is the peak sense of the word.
abstract.cn: 温度计在正午停止上升然后回落，那个停住的位置就是这个词的峰值义。

abstract.en: Every scale has two ends; maximum is the end you reach when nothing more can be added.
abstract.cn: 每把尺子都有两端，maximum 就是再也加不上去的那一端。

examples.en: The tank holds a maximum of fifty litres.
examples.cn: 这个油箱最多装五十升。

examples.en: The engine was running at maximum speed.
examples.cn: 发动机正以最高转速运转。

examples.en: Demand for water reaches its maximum in midsummer.
examples.cn: 对水的需求在盛夏达到峰值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克西姆」——把「麦克」一路推到顶格，就是最大值；记住 maximum 是最值里的最高那一格。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）的最高级 maximus，其中性形式 maximum 被英语原样借用；同族词多含 max- 或 magn-，都与「大」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the top of a scale; from that top value the senses split into the adjective use, the peak reached in time, and the mathematical maximum.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是量尺的顶端；从「顶端数值」分出形容词用法、时间上的峰值，以及数学上的极大值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle stopping at the last red mark on a dial, unable to go higher.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在表盘最后一格红色刻度上，再往上就推不动了。

branches.en: a fuel gauge pinned at the last mark
branches.cn: 油表指针顶在最后一格

branches.en: a runner's speed curve flattening at the top
branches.cn: 跑者速度曲线在顶端变平

branches.en: a speed limit sign naming the top allowed rate
branches.cn: 限速牌标出允许的最高速率

branches.en: a river cresting at noon and then dropping
branches.cn: 河水在正午涨到最高，随后下落

branches.en: a graph whose curve turns over near the middle
branches.cn: 曲线在图中间附近转向

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin adjective of size, its superlative, and the endings that turn that stem into nouns, adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示大小的拉丁形容词、它的最高级，以及把词干变成名词、形容词和动词的几种词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

maximus 是 magnus 的最高级形式。
maximum 是中性形式，可以作名词。
maximum 中的 -imum 是中性词尾。
maximal 由 max- 加 -al 构成。

definition_zh: 编辑；主编；剪辑师
definition_en: a person who prepares text, a newspaper or a film for publication or release, or who is in charge of a publication
core_image: 稿纸上满是红笔批注，编辑还在删掉一句
scene: 稿纸上满是红笔批注，编辑还在删掉一句。 The editor cut a whole paragraph before the issue closed.
sceneCN: 这里 editor 是「编辑」（第 1 个义项：整理文本、准备出版的人）；句意为截稿前编辑删掉了整整一段。图中可辨识物件：稿纸、红笔批注、删去的段落。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「编辑的；社论」

senses.title: A person who prepares text
senses.definition: a person whose job is to prepare written material for publication by correcting, cutting and arranging it
senses.definitionCN: 以修改、删减和编排书面材料来准备出版为职业的人
senses.example: The editor cut a whole paragraph before the issue closed.
senses.exampleCN: 截稿前编辑删掉了整整一段。
senses.why: Latin editor meant one who brings forth; the modern editor brings a text out into the world in its final shape.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 editor 意为「把东西拿出来的人」；现代编辑就是把文本以最终形态带到世人面前的人。

senses.title: The person in charge of a publication
senses.titleCN: 主编：负责一份出版物的人
senses.definition: the senior person who decides what a newspaper, magazine or series will contain
senses.definitionCN: 决定报纸、杂志或丛书内容的资深负责人
senses.example: The editor refused to print the story without a second source.
senses.exampleCN: 没有第二个消息来源，主编拒绝刊登这篇报道。
senses.why: Bringing forth a paper belongs to the person at the top of the desk, so editor also names the post of command.
senses.whyCN: 把一份报纸拿出来，是编辑部最高负责人的职责，于是 editor 也指这个指挥职位。

senses.title: A person who cuts film or sound
senses.titleCN: 剪辑师：剪辑影像或声音的人
senses.definition: a person who selects and arranges shots, scenes or sound recordings for a film, video or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 为电影、视频或广播挑选与编排镜头、场景或录音的人
senses.example: The film editor built the chase from forty separate shots.
senses.exampleCN: 剪辑师用四十个独立镜头剪出了这场追逐。
senses.why: Film is brought forth by cutting and joining, so the worker who does that keeps the old title of one who brings forth.
senses.whyCN: 电影是靠剪接与拼接「拿出来」的，做这活的人便沿用了「拿出者」的旧称。

intro.en: Editor is Latin in form and meaning: one who brings something forth for others.
intro.cn: editor 的形态与含义都来自拉丁语：把某物拿出来给别人的人。

items.en: Dare meant to give, and it is the second element of the publishing verb.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，是出版类动词的第二个成分。

items.en: E plus dare formed edere, to give out or bring forth.
items.cn: e- 加 dare 构成 edere，意为「发出、拿出」。

items.en: Editor was the person noun for one who brings forth or publishes.
items.cn: editor 是表示「拿出者、出版者」的指人名词。

items.en: English borrowed editor for a publisher or writer, and the word later narrowed to the person who prepares text.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 editor，指出版者或作者，后来窄化为整理文本的人。

items.en: Newspapers and film added the commanding and the cutting senses, while the root meaning stayed visible.
items.cn: 报纸与电影加入了「负责人」与「剪辑」两义，而词根含义仍然可见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the publishing family; the near-meaning group gathers people who work on texts and images.
note.cn: 形近组收出版词族；近义组收处理文本与影像的人。

entries.definition: One published version or print run of a work.
entries.definitionCN: 一件作品的一种出版版本或一次印量。

entries.definition: An adjective for editing, or a newspaper's opinion piece.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指编辑的；也指报纸评论文章。

entries.definition: The position or period of being an editor.
entries.definitionCN: 编辑的职位或任期。

entries.definition: A person who checks text for errors before printing.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷前检查文本错误的人。

entries.definition: A person who gathers news for a paper or broadcast.
entries.definitionCN: 为报纸或广播采集新闻的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks follow the person who brings text, papers and films out into the world.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子跟着那个把文本、报纸与电影带到世人面前的人。

normal.en: Editor means one who brings forth; the red pen is the tool of bringing forth.
normal.cn: editor 意为「拿出者」；红笔就是拿出的工具。

normal.en: The editor-in-chief brings out the whole paper, not one page.
normal.cn: 主编拿出的是整份报纸，而不是一页。

normal.en: A film editor brings out a story by choosing which shots survive.
normal.cn: 电影剪辑师通过决定哪些镜头存活，把一个故事拿出来。

normal.en: Edit, editor, edition, editorial: one giving-out family.
normal.cn: edit、editor、edition、editorial：同一个「拿出」词族。

normal.en: A copy editor saves the reader from the writer's mistakes.
normal.cn: 文字编辑替读者挡住作者的错。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifting a clean page out of a pile of marked drafts.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从一摞批注稿中抽出一张干净的纸。

abstract.en: The same lifting can produce a book, a newspaper, a film, or a corrected paragraph.
abstract.cn: 同一次「抽出」可以产出一本书、一份报纸、一部电影，或一个改好的段落。

abstract.en: Editor means someone decides what version of a thing the world will see.
abstract.cn: editor 意味着由某人决定世人将看到这东西的哪个版本。

examples.en: The editor cut a whole paragraph before the issue closed.
examples.cn: 截稿前编辑删掉了整整一段。

examples.en: The editor refused to print the story without a second source.
examples.cn: 没有第二个消息来源，主编拒绝刊登这篇报道。

examples.en: The film editor built the chase from forty separate shots.
examples.cn: 剪辑师用四十个独立镜头剪出了这场追逐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「埃迪特」——稿纸上红笔一圈，整段被删

root: 拉丁语 editor「拿出者、出版者」由 edere「发出、出版」派生，edere 又由 e-「出」加 dare「给」构成；十七世纪进入英语，后窄化为整理文本的人。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of editor: the person who prepares text, the person in charge of a publication, and the person who cuts film or sound.
sensesIntro.cn: editor 的三个义项：整理文本的人、负责一份出版物的人，以及剪辑影像或声音的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifts one clean page out of a pile of marked drafts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从一摞批注稿中抽出一张干净的纸。

branches.en: THE TEXT: correcting and arranging words for publication.
branches.cn: 文本线：为出版而修改与编排文字。

branches.en: THE DESK: deciding what a whole publication contains.
branches.cn: 编辑部线：决定整份出版物的内容。

branches.en: THE CUT: choosing which shots or sounds survive.
branches.cn: 剪辑线：决定哪些镜头或声音留存。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY: the same person may both polish the text and command the desk.
branches.cn: 权威线：同一个人可能既打磨文本又指挥编辑部。

branches.en: THE SELECTION: in words and in film, the job is choosing what to keep.
branches.cn: 取舍线：无论文字还是电影，这份工作都是决定留下什么。

intro.en: Editor is a Latin agent noun; English adds -ial, -ship and plural endings.
intro.cn: editor 是拉丁语施事名词，英语加 -ial、-ship 与复数词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin edere and editor are recorded, and the agent suffix -or is visible in both Latin and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 edere 与 editor 均有记录，施事后缀 -or 在拉丁语与英语中都可见。

items.example: It is the base of the publishing verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是出版类动词的词基。

definition_zh: 困惑；混乱；混淆；骚动
definition_en: a state of not understanding what is happening, or a lack of order
core_image: 雾中的一群人，各朝不同的方向走
scene: 停电之后，大厅里的人不知该往哪个出口走。 The sudden darkness caused confusion in the hall.
sceneCN: 这里 confusion 指「混乱」（第 2 个义项：秩序被打乱的状态）；句意是突然的黑暗在大厅里引起了混乱。

senses.title: A puzzled mind
senses.definition: the feeling of not being able to understand or decide
senses.definitionCN: 无法理解或无法决定的感受
senses.example: His answer left me in complete confusion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答让我完全糊涂了。
senses.why: A mind given too many directions at once stops choosing any.
senses.whyCN: 脑子同时收到太多方向，就一个也不选了。

senses.title: A lack of order
senses.definition: a situation in which things are disordered and hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 事物秩序被打乱、难以控制的情形
senses.example: The room was in complete confusion after the move.
senses.exampleCN: 搬完之后房间里一片混乱。
senses.why: When every object leaves its place, the eye loses its map.
senses.whyCN: 每样东西都离开原位，眼睛就失去了地图。

senses.title: Mixing two things up
senses.definition: the act of treating two different things as the same
senses.definitionCN: 把两样不同的事物当成同一样
senses.example: The confusion of the two names caused real trouble.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个名称的混淆带来了真正的麻烦。
senses.why: A name is a handle, and two handles on one door lead to the wrong room.
senses.whyCN: 名字是把手，一扇门上装两个把手就会走错房间。

intro.en: Confusion comes from Latin confusio, a pouring together, from confundere, to pour together.
intro.cn: confusion 来自拉丁语 confusio，意为倒在一起，源自 confundere（混合倾倒）。

items.en: Fundere meant to pour something out.
items.cn: fundere 意为把某物倒出来。

items.en: Confundere meant to pour different things into one container.
items.cn: confundere 意为把不同的东西倒进同一个容器。

items.en: Confusio named the mixed and disordered result.
items.cn: confusio 指混合之后那种杂乱的结果。

items.en: French confusion applied the image to a disordered mind.
items.cn: 法语 confusion 把这个意象用于混乱的心思。

items.en: English confusion now covers puzzlement, disorder and mistaken identity.
items.cn: 英语 confusion 如今覆盖困惑、混乱与认错对象。

note.en: The look-alike group holds nouns with a similar ending, and the meaning group names other states of disorder or doubt.
note.cn: 形近组收的是词尾相近的名词，近义组列出其他表示混乱或疑惑的状态。

entries.definition: a judgement reached after thinking
entries.definitionCN: 结论；推论

entries.definition: a statement admitting a fault
entries.definitionCN: 坦白；供词

entries.definition: something given up in an argument
entries.definitionCN: 让步；特许

entries.definition: a state in which things are not properly arranged
entries.definitionCN: 混乱；失调

entries.definition: a state of complete and confusing disorder
entries.definitionCN: 完全的混乱

entries.definition: the feeling of being unable to understand
entries.definitionCN: 困惑；迷惑

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a crowd walking in different directions, then move to a moved room and to two names on one door.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从各走各的人群开始，再走到刚搬完的房间与一扇门上的两个名字。

normal.en: Confuse plus -ion turns the act of mixing into the state of being mixed.
normal.cn: confuse 加 -ion，就把混合的动作变成了混合的状态。

normal.en: Confusion is what a room looks like when every chair has forgotten its corner.
normal.cn: 混乱，就是每把椅子都忘了自己该在哪个角落的房间。

normal.en: A crowd in confusion moves fast and arrives nowhere.
normal.cn: 混乱中的人群走得很快，却哪里也到不了。

normal.en: The confusion of two names is a small mistake with a long shadow.
normal.cn: 两个名字的混淆是小错，却拖着长长的影子。

normal.en: Clear one fact at a time, and confusion begins to thin.
normal.cn: 一次弄清一个事实，混乱就开始变薄。

abstract.en: Picture a fog full of people facing different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一片雾里的人群面朝不同方向。

abstract.en: Picture a desk swept into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子被扫成一堆。

abstract.en: Picture two names written on one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门上写着两个名字。

examples.en: There was some confusion about the meeting time.
examples.cn: 关于会议时间有一些混乱。

examples.en: The new signs should clear up the confusion.
examples.cn: 新标志应该能消除这种困惑。

examples.en: In the confusion, nobody noticed the open gate.
examples.cn: 在一片混乱中，没人注意到敞开的大门。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confusion 记成 confuse（倒在一起）加 ion：东西全倒在一处，分不清彼此，就是混乱与困惑。

root: 源自拉丁语 confusio（con 一起 + fundere 倾倒），本义是混倒在一起，后引申为困惑、混乱与混淆。

sensesIntro.en: From liquids mixed in one vessel, to a mind without direction, and finally to two things taken for one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从倒进同一容器的液体，到失去方向的头脑，最后到把两样东西当成一样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foggy hall where everyone walks a different way.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片雾中的大厅，每个人走向不同方向。

branches.en: The mental sense is a person who cannot decide.
branches.cn: 心理义项是一个无法做决定的人。

branches.en: The physical sense is a space that has lost its order.
branches.cn: 物理义项是一个失去秩序的空间。

branches.en: The naming sense is two different things sharing one label.
branches.cn: 命名义项是两样不同的东西共用同一个标签。

branches.en: A disordered room and a disordered mind look surprisingly alike.
branches.cn: 杂乱的房间与杂乱的头脑，看起来出奇地像。

branches.en: Mixing up names is the smallest form of a larger mess.
branches.cn: 弄混名字，是更大混乱中最小的那一种。

intro.en: Confusion is Latin com-, together, plus fundere, to pour, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: confusion 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、fundere（倾倒）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pour base fus- also appears in fusion and refuse.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的倾倒词基 fus- 也出现在 fusion 与 refuse 中。

items.meaning: a state of disorder or doubt
items.exampleCN: 这个消息引起了很大的混乱。
这两张地图让旅行者犯糊涂。
每个人看上去都很困惑。

items.meaning: the joining of two things into one
items.example: The band plays a fusion of jazz and folk.
items.exampleCN: 这支乐队演奏爵士与民谣的融合。

items.example: She refused to sign the form.
A warm light suffused the room.
items.exampleCN: 温暖的光弥漫了整个房间。

definition_zh: 音调；语气；色调；风格
definition_en: the quality of a sound or voice, or the general mood and style of something
core_image: 同一句话的不同声调：声音里带着的颜色和态度
scene: 老师对学生的语气感到不满，说道： I don't like the tone of your answer just now.
sceneCN: 这里 tone 是「语气」（第 2 个义项：说话的方式和态度）；句意是老师不喜欢学生刚才回答的语气。

derivatives.zh: 由 tone 加 -ed 构成，义为「有……色调的；肌肉结实的」
由 tone 加 -er 构成，义为「调色剂；爽肤水」
mono-（单一）+ tone，义为「单调的声音」

senses.title: A quality of sound
senses.definition: a sound with a particular pitch or quality, especially of the voice or a musical instrument
senses.definitionCN: 具有特定音高或质感的声音，尤指人声或乐器声
senses.example: The piano has a rich, warm tone.
senses.exampleCN: 这架钢琴音色醇厚温暖。
senses.why: The core image of sound carrying color starts from the raw quality of a single note.
senses.whyCN: 声音自带「颜色」的核心意象，正始于单个音的质感。

senses.title: The manner of speaking
senses.definition: the way someone's voice shows their feelings or attitude when speaking
senses.definitionCN: 说话声音中流露出的情感或态度
senses.example: Her tone made it clear that she was angry.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气清楚地表明她生气了。
senses.why: The same words in different tones carry different attitudes, so sound quality turns into attitude.
senses.whyCN: 同样的话用不同声调说出来态度各异，于是声音质感引申为态度。

senses.title: A shade of color
senses.definition: a slight variety of a color, or the general effect of colors together
senses.definitionCN: 颜色的细微差异，或整体配色给人的效果
senses.example: The room is painted in soft earth tones.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了柔和的大地色调。
senses.why: Just as sound has tone, color was said to have its own tone, so the word crossed into color.
senses.whyCN: 声音有 tone，颜色也被说成有自己的 tone，一词跨入色彩领域。

senses.title: The general mood or style
senses.definition: the general feeling, mood, or style of a piece of writing, event, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 文章、事件或局面的整体情绪或风格
senses.example: The opening speech set a serious tone for the conference.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕致辞为会议定下了严肃的基调。
senses.why: The overall attitude of a talk is its tone at scale, from one sentence to a whole event.
senses.whyCN: 整场讲话的态度就是放大的语气，从一个句子扩展到整个事件。

senses.title: Firmness of the body
senses.definition: the normal firmness or strength of muscles and tissues
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉和组织的正常紧实度与力量
senses.example: Swimming improves muscle tone.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳能改善肌肉的紧实度。
senses.why: A body in good condition was said to be in good tone, like an instrument in tune.
senses.whyCN: 身体状态好被说成「tone 好」，如同乐器音准良好。

senses.title: To soften or strengthen
senses.definition: to make a color, feeling, or body less strong or more firm
senses.definitionCN: 使颜色、情绪变得柔和，或使身体变得结实
senses.example: You should tone down your criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该缓和一下批评的措辞。
senses.why: Adjusting a tone in music means changing its strength, so the verb means to adjust.
senses.whyCN: 调整乐音就是改变其强度，动词义由此表示「调节」。

intro.en: Tone comes through French from Latin tonus, which itself is from Greek tonos meaning 'a stretching'.
intro.cn: tone 经法语来自拉丁语 tonus，后者又源自希腊语 tonos，本义「拉伸」。

items.en: The root *ten- meant 'to stretch', seen in many English words like extend.
items.cn: 词根 *ten- 意为「拉伸」，与 extend 等许多词同源。

items.en: Tonos meant a stretching, tension, or the pitch of a voice.
items.cn: 希腊语 tonos 意为拉伸、张力，或人声的音高。

items.en: Tonus kept the sense of sound or pitch in learned use.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tonus 保留了声音、音高的含义。

items.en: Ton passed into French with the meaning of sound and voice quality.
items.cn: ton 进入法语，意为声音、嗓音质地。

items.en: Tone entered English for musical sound, then spread to color, mood, and health.
items.cn: 十四世纪 tone 进入英语指乐音，后扩展到色彩、情绪与健康。

note.en: Spelling neighbors of tone, and words sharing the sound-and-mood field.
note.cn: 与 tone 拼写相近的词，以及同属声音与情绪义场的词。

entries.definition: a unit of weight
entries.definitionCN: 吨，重量单位，只是与 tone 拼写相近，词源迥异

entries.definition: the organ of speech and taste
entries.definitionCN: 舌头；语言，拼写相近但与 tone 无词源关联

entries.definition: without tone or expression
entries.definitionCN: 无音调的；缺乏表情的，由 tone 加后缀构成

entries.definition: giving strength; a strengthening drink
entries.definitionCN: 滋补的；补药，与 tone 同出希腊词根「拉伸」

entries.definition: how high or low a sound is
entries.definitionCN: 音高，指声音的高低，tone 更强调音的质感

entries.definition: the feeling of a place or time
entries.definitionCN: 情绪；氛围，与 tone 的「基调」义相近

entries.definition: a slight variety of a color
entries.definitionCN: 色度；深浅层次，与 tone 的「色调」义重叠

entries.definition: the way of pronouncing words
entries.definitionCN: 口音；重音，同样属于说话方式

normalIntro.en: Use the Greek stretch root and everyday phrases to fix the word.
normalIntro.cn: 用希腊「拉伸」词根和日常搭配来固定这个词。

normal.en: tone shares the root ten- (stretch) with extend
normal.cn: tone 与 extend 同出词根 ten-（拉伸），声音是被「拉紧」发出的

normal.en: set the tone = decide the general feeling
normal.cn: set the tone（定基调）是开场、开篇的常用说法

normal.en: tone down = make it softer
normal.cn: tone down（缓和）常用于批评、色彩、新闻措辞

normal.en: muscle tone = how firm your muscles are
normal.cn: muscle tone 指肌肉紧实度，健身语境常见

normal.en: skin tone = the color of your skin
normal.cn: skin tone 指肤色，化妆品语境高频词

abstract.en: Hear one violin note glowing with its own color
abstract.cn: 听小提琴的一个音泛出它独有的颜色

abstract.en: Feel your voice tense like a stretched string when angry
abstract.cn: 体会生气时嗓音如拉紧的琴弦般紧绷

abstract.en: See a room's mood change when the wall color tones down
abstract.cn: 看墙面色调变柔时房间氛围随之改变

examples.en: Please speak in a calm tone.
examples.cn: 请用平静的语气说话。

examples.en: The novelist toned down the violence in the final draft.
examples.cn: 小说家在终稿中淡化了暴力描写。

examples.en: Exercise tones the muscles and lifts the mood.
examples.cn: 锻炼使肌肉紧实，也提振情绪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「痛」——同样一句「你真棒」，用「痛」的口气说出来就是嘲讽；记住 tone 就是声音里的态度。

root: 希腊语 tonos（拉伸、张力）→ 拉丁语 tonus（音）→ 古法语 ton → 英语 tone。与词根 ten-（拉）同族，extend、tension、tendon 均为亲戚。

sensesIntro.en: From the pitch of one sound to the attitude in a voice, then to color, mood, and body strength.
sensesIntro.cn: 从单个乐音的音高，到嗓音中的态度，再扩展到色彩、基调与身体状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stretched string giving off colored sound
core.cn: 核心意象：拉紧的弦发出带着颜色的声音

definition_zh: 无处；没有地方；毫无进展；偏远之地；远不及
definition_en: in or to no place at all; also used of a remote place and of a complete lack of progress
core_image: 一张地图上所有道路都走到尽头，前方再没有可以落脚的地方
scene: 夜里车在荒原上抛了锚，四周只有风声和黑黢黢的草。 After two hours of walking, they found themselves nowhere near the village.
sceneCN: 这里是「远不及、离……还很远」（第 4 个义项：nowhere near 表示差得很远）；句意为走了两个小时，他们离村子还远得很。荒原与抛锚的车把「没有地方」的字面感先立了起来。

pos.zh: 偏远的地方（多见于 the middle of nowhere）

derivatives.zh: 由 nowhere 与 -ville 拼合的口语造词，指偏远又乏味的地方
