senses.title: In or to no place
senses.definition: in or to no place at all
senses.definitionCN: 在任何地方都不存在，或不到任何地方
senses.example: The keys were nowhere in the room.
senses.exampleCN: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。
senses.why: The word simply fused no with where, so it negates place itself: no location answers the question.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是把 no 与 where 直接焊在一起，否定的是地点本身：没有任何一个位置能回答「在哪里」。

senses.title: To make no progress
senses.definition: to fail to make any progress or reach any result
senses.definitionCN: 没能取得任何进展或结果
senses.example: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 和他争辩毫无用处。
senses.why: If the destination is no place, movement toward it can only end without arrival, which is how the word came to mean no result.
senses.whyCN: 既然目的地是「没有地方」，朝它走就永远到不了，于是这个词引申为「没有结果」。

senses.title: A remote and empty place
senses.definition: a place far from towns and hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 远离城镇、难以抵达的地方
senses.example: They built a cabin in the middle of nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在荒郊野外盖了一间小木屋。
senses.why: When a location is so far out that it feels like no place at all, the negated word becomes a name for remoteness itself.
senses.whyCN: 当某个地方远得像是「根本不存在」时，这个否定词就反过来成了「偏远」的代称。

senses.title: Far from reaching a standard
senses.definition: used before near or close to say that something is far from a target
senses.definitionCN: 用在 near 或 close 前，表示离目标差得很远
senses.example: The project is nowhere near finished.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目离完工还差得远。
senses.why: The same spatial gap that produced no place is reused as a gap in degree, so distance in space turns into distance from a standard.
senses.whyCN: 造出「没有地方」的那个空间落差被挪来表示程度差距：空间的距离变成了与标准的距离。

intro.en: Nowhere is a compound of two Old English words, na and hwaer, and it has kept its literal shape for centuries.
intro.cn: nowhere 由两个古英语词 na 与 hwaer 复合而成，几个世纪以来一直保持着字面的构造。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not any.
items.cn: na 是朴素的否定词，意为「没有、一点也不」。

items.en: Hwaer was the question word for place, the ancestor of where.
items.cn: hwaer 是询问地点的疑问词，是 where 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the compound as nawher or nowher, still spelling out both halves.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个复合词写作 nawher 或 nowher，两半仍看得清楚。

items.en: Early modern printers settled on nowhere, and the word also began to name remote places.
items.cn: 近代早期的印刷者把拼写固定为 nowhere，这个词也开始用来指偏远之地。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative senses of no result and far from a standard, as in get nowhere and nowhere near.
items.cn: 现代英语再加上「没有结果」与「远不及」两个比喻义，如 get nowhere 与 nowhere near。

note.en: The look-alike group collects place adverbs built on where; the near-meaning group collects words for remoteness and for useless effort.
note.cn: 形近组收由 where 构成的同族地点副词，近义组收表示偏远与徒劳的词。

entries.definition: In or to a place that is not named.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到某个未指明的地方。

entries.definition: In or to any place at all.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何地方。

entries.definition: In or to all places.
entries.definitionCN: 到处；各处。

entries.definition: In or to another place.
entries.definitionCN: 在或到别处。

entries.definition: Far away from towns and people.
entries.definitionCN: 远离城镇与人群的。

entries.definition: Cut off from others and hard to reach.
entries.definitionCN: 与外界隔绝、难以抵达的。

entries.definition: In a way that produces no result.
entries.definitionCN: 以毫无结果的方式。

entries.definition: A wild area with no towns or roads.
entries.definitionCN: 没有城镇与道路的荒野。

normalIntro.en: No plus where spells out no place; from that blank the word grows the senses of no result and far from a mark.
normalIntro.cn: no 与 where 一拼就写出「没有地方」；从这个空白里又长出「没有结果」与「差得远」。

normal.en: Nowhere is no plus where, so its literal meaning is not any place.
normal.cn: nowhere 就是 no 加 where，字面意思是不在任何地方。

normal.en: Because the destination is no place, get nowhere means you never arrive at a result.
normal.cn: 因为终点就是「没有地方」，所以 get nowhere 指永远到不了结果。

normal.en: Nowhere near keeps the same gap but measures distance from a target, not from a town.
normal.cn: nowhere near 保留同一个落差，只是量的是与目标的距离，而不是与城镇的距离。

normal.en: The middle of nowhere turns the negative into a name for the emptiest place around.
normal.cn: the middle of nowhere 把这个否定词反过来当成最空旷之处的名字。

normal.en: Spell it as one word: there is no space between no and where.
normal.cn: 拼写时写成一个词，no 与 where 之间不留空格。

abstract.en: A road ends in open grass: every direction has been walked and none leads anywhere.
abstract.cn: 一条路在荒草里到头：每个方向都走过了，哪儿也去不了。

abstract.en: Nowhere is the map's way of drawing an absence, a blank where a name should be.
abstract.cn: nowhere 是地图画「空缺」的方式：本该写名字的地方留了一片空白。

abstract.en: The same word can lose a place and lose a result, because both are destinations that never arrive.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能失去地点，也能失去结果，因为两者都是永远抵达不了的终点。

examples.en: The keys were nowhere in the room.
examples.cn: 钥匙在房间里哪儿都找不到。

examples.en: Arguing with him gets you nowhere.
examples.cn: 和他争辩毫无用处。

examples.en: The project is nowhere near finished.
examples.cn: 这个项目离完工还差得远。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「闹胃」——找不到地方吃饭，胃里闹得慌；记住 nowhere 是无处。

root: 古英语 na（不）与 hwær（何处）复合，字面即「何处都没有」；同族词为 somewhere、anywhere、everywhere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the absence of a place; the senses move from literal no place to no progress, a remote spot, and a gap in degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有地点」；义项先落在空间上的无处，再引申为没有进展、偏远之地，以及程度上的远不及。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a road that runs out at the edge of open grass, with no name on the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条路在荒草边缘走到尽头，地图上也没有名字。

branches.en: keys missing from every drawer in the room
branches.cn: 钥匙翻遍房间每个抽屉都不见

branches.en: a map with a blank space where a village should be
branches.cn: 本该标着村庄的地图却是一片空白

branches.en: two people arguing until both are tired
branches.cn: 两个人争到都累了也没个结果

branches.en: a cabin standing alone beyond the last road
branches.cn: 最后一道路尽头之外孤零零的小屋

branches.en: an unfinished bridge far from the plan
branches.cn: 与图纸相去甚远的半截桥

intro.en: The word is built from the Old English negative na and the question word hwaer; it has no Latin root, and its family is a row of place adverbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的否定词 na 与疑问词 hwær 组成，没有拉丁词根，同族是一整排地点副词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: place, as in somewhere or anywhere

definition_zh: 倒塌；崩溃；倒下
definition_en: to fall down suddenly, to fail completely, or to fall down because of illness or weakness
core_image: 一座楼在几秒之内塌成一堆瓦砾
scene: 旧仓库的屋顶在雨里撑不住了。 The old roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
sceneCN: 这里 collapse 指「倒塌」（第 1 个义项：突然塌下）；句意是旧屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。

senses.title: Fall down suddenly
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of pressure or a loss of support
senses.definitionCN: 因压力或失去支撑而突然塌下
senses.example: The roof collapsed under the weight of snow.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶在积雪的重压下塌了。
senses.why: The Latin base meant to fall together, which is exactly what a building does.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为一起倒下，这正是一栋楼倒塌的样子。

senses.title: Fail completely
senses.definition: to fail suddenly and completely, as a system or a plan does
senses.definitionCN: 像制度或计划那样突然彻底失败
senses.example: The talks collapsed after two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈两小时后破裂了。
senses.why: An argument can fall down like a wall when its supports give way.
senses.whyCN: 论证的支撑一断，也会像墙一样倒下。

senses.title: Fall down from weakness
senses.definition: to fall down suddenly because of illness, injury or tiredness
senses.definitionCN: 因病、受伤或疲劳突然倒下
senses.example: He collapsed at the end of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他在比赛终点倒下了。
senses.why: The body loses its support just as a structure does.
senses.whyCN: 身体像建筑物一样失去支撑。

intro.en: Collapse comes from Latin collabi, from com- together and labi, to slip or fall.
intro.cn: collapse 出自拉丁语 collabi，由 com-（一起）与 labi（滑落、倒下）组成。

items.en: Labi meant to slip, slide or fall.
items.cn: labi 意为滑、滑落或倒下。

items.en: Collabi described falling down in a heap.
items.cn: collabi 描述塌成一堆。

items.en: The participle collapsus was used of ruined buildings.
items.cn: 分词 collapsus 用于描述毁坏的建筑。

items.en: English collapse first described a building giving way.
items.cn: 英语 collapse 最初描述建筑垮塌。

items.en: Medicine and economics extended it to bodies and systems.
items.cn: 医学与经济学把它扩展到身体与制度。

note.en: The look-alike group holds Latin-shaped words with similar endings, while the meaning group names ways of breaking down or losing strength.
note.cn: 形近组收的是结尾相似、带拉丁形态的词，近义组列出碎裂与失去支撑的说法。

entries.definition: to pass, as time does
entries.definitionCN: 像时间那样流逝

entries.definition: to gather pages into the correct order
entries.definitionCN: 把书页按正确顺序整理

entries.definition: the hiding of the sun or moon by another body
entries.definitionCN: 太阳或月亮被另一天体遮住

entries.definition: to break into small pieces over time
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐碎成小块

entries.definition: to go down below a surface
entries.definitionCN: 沉到表面以下

entries.definition: to lose consciousness for a short time
entries.definitionCN: 短时间失去知觉

normalIntro.en: These hooks work from the Latin picture of falling together, then apply it to walls, plans and bodies.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一起倒下的拉丁画面出发，再挪到墙、计划与身体上。

normal.en: Collapse hides the Latin verb labi, to slip, so the word pictures a slide downward.
normal.cn: collapse 里藏着拉丁动词 labi（滑落），画面就是往下滑。

normal.en: The prefix com- means together, so everything falls at once.
normal.cn: 前缀 com- 意为一起，所以是所有东西同时倒下。

normal.en: A roof, a deal and a runner can all collapse in one second.
normal.cn: 屋顶、交易和奔跑者都可能在刹那间垮掉。

normal.en: Add -ible and collapsible means able to be folded down.
normal.cn: 加上 -ible，collapsible 就是能被折下来的。

normal.en: The noun keeps the same shape as the verb, so no ending is needed.
normal.cn: 名词与动词同形，不必另加词尾。

abstract.en: Picture a wall folding inward in a cloud of dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙在尘土中向内折倒。

abstract.en: Picture a row of numbers on a screen suddenly turning blank.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上的一排数字突然变成空白。

abstract.en: Picture a runner taking one more step and then folding to the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象奔跑者又迈一步，然后蜷倒在地。

examples.en: The bridge collapsed during the storm.
examples.cn: 那座桥在暴风雨中坍塌了。

examples.en: The company collapsed after losing its main investor.
examples.cn: 这家公司在失去主要投资人后垮掉了。

examples.en: She collapsed with tiredness after the long flight.
examples.cn: 长途飞行后她累得倒下了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 collapse 记成 com 加 lapse：所有东西一起滑落，就是塌掉。

root: 源自拉丁语 collabi，com-（一起）加 labi（滑落），本指建筑塌成一堆，后引申为制度失败与身体倒下。

sensesIntro.en: From a roof falling in to a plan breaking down, and then to a body that can no longer stand.
sensesIntro.cn: 从屋顶塌下，到计划破裂，再到再也站不住的身体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a structure losing its support and folding into a heap.
core.cn: 核心意象：结构失去支撑，折成一堆。

branches.en: The building sense is the oldest and most physical.
branches.cn: 建筑义最古老，也最具体。

branches.en: A plan fails the way a wall gives way.
branches.cn: 计划失败，就像墙失去支撑。

branches.en: The body sense borrows the same loss of support.
branches.cn: 身体义借用的同样是支撑的丧失。

branches.en: Both a roof and a person can fall in one sudden movement.
branches.cn: 屋顶和人都会在一个突然的动作中倒下。

branches.en: Systems and bodies both need support to keep standing.
branches.cn: 制度与身体都需要支撑才能立住。

intro.en: Collapse belongs to the Latin labi family, which also gives lapse, elapse and relapse.
intro.cn: collapse 属于拉丁语 labi 词族，这一族还给出 lapse、elapse 与 relapse。

latinIntro.en: The base labi, to slip, is the living element behind the whole group.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 labi（滑落）是整组词背后活的成分。

items.meaning: more than one collapse, or it falls down
items.example: The old wall collapses in heavy rain.
items.exampleCN: 这堵旧墙在大雨中塌下。

items.example: The tent collapsed in the wind.

items.exampleCN: 他们逃离了正在倒塌的建筑。

items.meaning: able to be folded or pushed down
items.exampleCN: 她带着一只可折叠的杯子。

items.meaning: a small failure or a passing of time
items.example: A lapse in attention caused the error.
items.exampleCN: 一次走神造成了这个错误。

items.example: Three hours elapsed before the call came.
items.exampleCN: 三个小时过去，电话才来。

items.meaning: to fall back into illness or a bad habit
items.example: He relapsed after a week of rest.
items.exampleCN: 休息一周后他又复发了。

items.meaning: a body part slipping out of place
items.example: The doctor treated a minor prolapse.
items.exampleCN: 医生治疗了一处轻微的脱垂。

latinEntries.example: Latin collabi is built from com- and labi.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 collabi 由 com- 与 labi 构成。

latinEntries.example: The verb labi also lies behind relapse.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 动词 labi 也藏在 relapse 背后。

definition_zh: 惩罚；刑罚；处罚；严厉对待：因过错而施加的痛苦或损失，也指行为主义中用以降低行为频率的后果
definition_en: pain, loss or other hardship imposed for a fault, including the consequence used in behaviourism to make an act less frequent
core_image: 一只伸向热炉的手被烫得立刻缩回，炉子原地未动，退缩的是那只手
scene: 手刚碰到热炉边缘就猛地缩回，炉子原地未动。 The punishment was immediate, and the child never reached for the stove again.
sceneCN: 这里指因过错而施加的痛苦后果（第 1 个义项：一般意义上的惩罚）；句意为惩罚来得即时，孩子此后再也没有伸手去碰炉子；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 惩罚；处罚（可数与不可数兼有）
刑罚；体罚（法律或行为主义用法）

forms.label: 复数（指具体处罚种类或次数）

derivatives.zh: punire 去词尾 → 施加惩罚，语义保留「使付出代价」
punire + -ive（具有……性质的）→ 以惩罚为目的的
punish + -ing（现在分词形容词）→ 令人疲惫不堪的，语义偏移为「折磨人的」
in-（不） + poena（惩罚）→ 免受惩罚，词根相同而前缀相反

senses.title: Pain imposed for a fault
senses.titleCN: 因过错而施加的痛苦或损失
senses.definition: something unpleasant imposed on a person because of a wrong or a broken rule
senses.definitionCN: 因错误或违反规则而加在人身上的不快后果
senses.example: The punishment for the prank was a week without a bicycle.
senses.exampleCN: 恶作剧的惩罚是一周不许骑车。
senses.why: Latin poena meant 'penalty, compensation', so punishment begins as a price paid for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、补偿」，惩罚最初就是为过错付出的代价。

senses.title: A legal penalty
senses.definition: a penalty imposed by a court for an offence, such as a fine, imprisonment or loss of rights
senses.definitionCN: 法院对罪行施加的罚金、监禁或剥夺权利等处罚
senses.example: The punishment for the offence was reduced on appeal.
senses.exampleCN: 该项罪行的刑罚在上诉后被减轻。
senses.why: law formalised the payment: the community takes something from the offender in return for the harm.
senses.whyCN: 法律把这种偿付形式化：社群从违法者那里取走某物，以抵偿损害。

senses.title: A penalty under rules
senses.definition: a penalty imposed within a game, school or workplace for breaking its rules
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、学校或工作场所内因违反规则而施加的处罚
senses.example: The referee's punishment was a penalty kick.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判的处罚是一个点球。
senses.why: any rule-governed group needs a price for breaking rules, and the same word covers it.
senses.whyCN: 任何受规则约束的群体都需要为违规定一个代价，同一个词便覆盖了它。

senses.title: Harsh treatment
senses.definition: rough, exhausting or cruel treatment that goes beyond any stated rule
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何明文规则的粗暴、耗人或不人道对待
senses.example: The old boat took a punishment in every storm.
senses.exampleCN: 这条旧船在每场风暴中都遭到重创。
senses.why: when no rule is stated, the word still names harm inflicted, and it extends to objects and bodies.
senses.whyCN: 没有明文规则时，这个词仍指被施加的伤害，并扩展到物体与身体。

senses.title: The behaviourist consequence
senses.titleCN: 行为主义中降低行为频率的后果
senses.definition: a consequence that makes a behaviour less likely to recur, in contrast with reinforcement
senses.definitionCN: 使行为更不可能再次发生的后果，与强化相对
senses.example: The punishment reduced the number of late arrivals but also raised absenteeism.
senses.exampleCN: 惩罚减少了迟到次数，却也提高了缺勤率。
senses.why: psychology needed the exact opposite of reinforcement, and it reused the everyday word for paying for a wrong.
senses.whyCN: 心理学需要强化的精确对立面，便复用了这个表示「为过错付出代价」的日常词。

senses.title: Corporal punishment
senses.definition: physical punishment such as hitting, used especially of school or household discipline
senses.definitionCN: 殴打等身体惩罚，尤指学校或家庭管教
senses.example: Corporal punishment was banned in the district's schools.
senses.exampleCN: 该学区的学校禁止体罚。
senses.why: the body is the oldest surface on which a penalty is written, so the compound names that case directly.
senses.whyCN: 身体是最古老的书写惩罚的表面，因此这个复合词直接命名那种情形。

senses.title: A financial penalty
senses.definition: a sum of money exacted for a violation, delay or breach of contract
senses.definitionCN: 因违规、延误或违约而被收取的一笔钱
senses.example: The punishment for late filing was a fixed fee.
senses.exampleCN: 逾期申报的处罚是一笔固定费用。
senses.why: poena was originally a payment, so a fine is the most literal modern descendant.
senses.whyCN: poena 原本就是一种付款，因此罚款是这个词最字面的现代后裔。

senses.title: Self-punishment
senses.definition: harm a person inflicts on themselves out of guilt, shame or a sense of owed payment
senses.definitionCN: 出于内疚、羞耻或「应当偿付」之感而对自己施加的伤害
senses.example: His punishment was to give up the thing he loved most.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自我惩罚是放弃自己最爱的东西。
senses.why: if a wrong creates a debt, the debtor can be both the one who owes and the one who collects.
senses.whyCN: 如果过错产生债务，欠债者与收债者可以是同一个人。

intro.en: Punishment comes from Latin poena 'penalty, compensation' through the verb punire and Old French. The ultimate source is Greek poine 'penalty, recompense'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: punishment 经动词 punire 与古法语上溯拉丁 poena「罚金、补偿」。其最终来源是希腊 poine「惩罚、报偿」。年代为约数。

items.en: Poine meant 'penalty, recompense, blood-money'. The idea is payment for a wrong rather than correction of the offender.
items.cn: poine 意为「惩罚、报偿、血金」。其观念是为过错付款，而不是矫正犯错者。

items.en: Latin poena meant 'penalty, punishment, compensation'. It is the source of penal, penalty and impunity as well.
items.cn: 拉丁 poena 意为「罚金、惩罚、补偿」。它也是 penal、penalty 与 impunity 的来源。

items.en: Punire meant 'to punish, to avenge, to take vengeance for'. Its noun punitio named the act of punishing.
items.cn: punire 意为「惩罚、报仇、为……复仇」。其名词 punitio 指惩罚行为。

items.en: Old French punir and punissement carried the legal sense into English from the twelfth century onward.
items.cn: 古法语 punir 与 punissement 从 12 世纪起把法律义带入英语。

items.en: English punishment covered both the legal penalty and the general infliction of pain, and later the rough wear that objects endure.
items.cn: 英语 punishment 兼指法律刑罚与一般施加的痛苦，后来又指物体承受的粗暴损耗。

items.en: Reconstructed form (pre-Greek root): poine is often attached to an Indo-European root for 'payment, price', but that root is a reconstruction and no single pre-Greek form is demonstrated; the Greek noun itself is attested.
items.cn: 重构形式（希腊语之前的词根）：poine 常被挂到印欧语「付款、价格」词根上，但该词根属重构，也没有单一的前希腊语形式得到证明；这个希腊名词本身有书证。

note.en: Group one holds legal and formal relatives that are easily confused with the general word; group two holds other imposed consequences with a different purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是易与通称混淆的法律与正式同族词；第二组是目的不同的其他施加性后果。

entries.definition: The specific disadvantage attached to a rule or offence, such as a fine; punishment is the wider act or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则或罪行所附的具体不利后果，如罚款；punishment 是更宽的行为或制度。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'intended to punish'; it describes the aim of a measure, not the measure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以惩罚为目的」的形容词，描述措施的目的，而非措施本身。

entries.definition: Exemption from punishment, built with a negative prefix on the same Latin root; it is the opposite condition.
entries.definitionCN: 免受惩罚，在同一拉丁词根上加否定前缀，指相反的状态。

entries.definition: A penalty imposed by an authority or by states; it is formal and often collective, while punishment can be personal.
entries.definitionCN: 由权威或国家施加的处罚，正式且常为集体性；punishment 可以是个人性的。

entries.definition: Punishment understood as deserved payback; it stresses the balance of harm rather than the rule broken.
entries.definitionCN: 被理解为应得报偿的惩罚，强调伤害的平衡，而非被违反的规则。

entries.definition: Any result of an act, pleasant or not; it carries no judgment, whereas punishment implies a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 任何行为的结果，好坏皆可，不带评判；punishment 则含有过错之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real legal collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实法律搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: poena 'price paid': punishment is a price exacted for a wrong.
normal.cn: poena「付出的价钱」：惩罚就是为过错索取的价钱。

normal.en: The family runs punish, punishment, punitive, punishable, impunity.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 punish、punishment、punitive、punishable、impunity。

normal.en: Legal phrases pin the formal sense: capital punishment, corporal punishment, impose a punishment.
normal.cn: 法律搭配钉住正式义：死刑、体罚、施加惩罚。

normal.en: The prefix in impunity is negative, so impunity is the absence of the price.
normal.cn: impunity 里的前缀是否定的，因此 impunity 就是没有这笔价钱。

normal.en: The behaviourist pair is punishment and reward, moving frequency down and up.
normal.cn: 行为主义的配对是惩罚与奖励，分别把频率往下与往上推。

abstract.en: Picture a hand touching a hot stove and pulling back at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手碰到热炉，立刻缩回。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed over for a debt nobody wanted to pay.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据，为一笔没人想付的债开出。

abstract.en: Picture a judge and an offender both holding the same coin.
abstract.cn: 想象法官与犯错者同时握着同一枚硬币。

examples.en: The punishment must fit the offence, the old principle runs.
examples.cn: 古老的原则说，惩罚必须与罪行相称。

examples.en: Punishment alone rarely teaches the behaviour that should replace it.
examples.cn: 单靠惩罚很少能教会被替代的正确行为。

examples.en: The fine was a punishment for late payment, not a fee for service.
examples.cn: 这笔罚款是对迟付的惩罚，而非服务费。

dict_mnemonic.text: punish（惩罚）+ ment（名词）＝ 惩罚；记「手碰热炉，缩回的是手」。

root: 希腊 poine「惩罚、报偿」→ 拉丁 poena「罚金、补偿」→ punire「惩罚」→ 古法语 punir／punissement。poine 的希腊语之前来源不确定，与印欧语「付款、价格」词根的联系属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one price: a wrong creates a debt, the court collects it, a rule collects it, a body pays it, and psychology and conscience each keep a ledger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一笔价钱展开：过错产生一笔债，法庭来收，规则来收，身体来付，心理学与良心各自记着一本账。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand touches a hot stove, withdraws at once, and the stove has not moved.
core.cn: 核心意象：手碰到热炉，立刻缩回，炉子却原地未动。

branches.en: THE PRICE: a fault creates something owed, and punishment is the payment demanded.
branches.cn: 价钱：过错产生应偿之物，惩罚就是被索取的偿付。

branches.en: TWO COLLECTORS: a court and a rule-governed group both exact the price.
branches.cn: 两个收取者：法庭与受规则约束的群体都来收取这笔价钱。

branches.en: THE BODY: rough treatment and corporal discipline write the penalty on a body.
branches.cn: 身体：粗暴对待与体罚把惩罚写在身体上。

branches.en: TWO LEDGERS: behaviourism lowers frequency, and a fine lowers the bank balance.
branches.cn: 两本账：行为主义降低频率，罚款降低账户余额。

branches.en: THE SELF: when the debtor and the collector are one person, the punishment turns inward.
branches.cn: 自身：当欠债者与收债者同为一人，惩罚便转向内。

intro.en: Punishment is a Latin root plus an English noun suffix, and the root also builds the legal family of penalty, punitive and impunity.
intro.cn: punishment 是拉丁词根加英语名词后缀，这个词根还构成 penalty、punitive 与 impunity 这一法律词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin poena 'penalty' gives punire 'to punish' and punitio 'punishment'; the English suffix -ment names the act or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 poena「罚金」给出 punire「惩罚」与 punitio「惩罚」；英语后缀 -ment 命名行为或其结果。

items.example: The noun is the root of penalty and impunity too.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词也是 penalty 与 impunity 的词根。

items.structure: punire, punivi, punitum (Latin verb, fourth conjugation)
items.example: The verb carries the idea of collecting a debt.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词带着「收取债务」的意思。

items.example: The action noun is the Latin model behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动作名词是英语词背后的拉丁模板。

items.example: The verb is the everyday member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是词族中最日常的一员。

items.meaning: the act or result of punishing
items.example: The suffix turns the act into a countable thing.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把行为变成可计数之物。

items.example: The adjective marks purpose rather than act.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记目的，而非行为。

items.example: The suffix marks what the law can reach.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记法律能触及的范围。

items.example: The negative prefix reverses the whole idea.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把整个观念反过来。

items.meaning: a specific disadvantage for an offence
items.meaningCN: 对过错的具体不利后果
items.example: The word is the countable cousin of punishment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是 punishment 的可计数近亲。

definition_zh: 缺乏；不足；缺少
definition_en: the state of not having something, or to be without something that is needed
core_image: 一只空碗摆在桌上，该有的东西一样也没盛上
scene: 厨房的储物柜被拉开，里面只剩几个空罐子。 The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
sceneCN: 这里是「缺少、不足」（第 1 个义项：名词，指某物不存在或数量不够）；句意为蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。图中可辨识物件：空罐子、空碗、打开的橱柜。

derivatives.zh: 由 lack 加 -ing 构成，义为「缺少的；不足的」
由 lack 与 luster（光泽）复合而成，义为「暗淡的；平淡无奇的」

senses.title: The state of not having enough of something
senses.definition: the state of not having something, or of not having enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 某物不存在或数量不够的状态
senses.example: The project was delayed by a lack of funds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目因为资金不足而推迟。
senses.why: Lack names an empty place where something should be; the word points at the gap rather than at any object.
senses.whyCN: lack 指的是本该有东西却空着的位置，它指向的是那个缺口，而不是任何具体物件。

senses.title: To be without something needed
senses.definition: to have none of something, or not enough of it
senses.definitionCN: 完全没有某物，或某物的量不够
senses.example: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
senses.exampleCN: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。
senses.why: The noun was turned into a verb without adding a suffix, so 'to lack' is simply to be in the state the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 名词原样转成动词，没有加后缀，所以 to lack 就是处在名词所指的那种「空着」的状态。

senses.title: A shortage that causes trouble
senses.definition: a shortage of something necessary, especially one that causes difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 必要之物短缺，尤指因此造成困难的情形
senses.example: The old town suffers from a lack of clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老城饱受清洁水源短缺之苦。
senses.why: When the missing thing is necessary, the gap becomes a problem, and English extends lack from a neutral absence to a damaging shortage.
senses.whyCN: 当缺的是必需品时，那个缺口就成了麻烦，英语便从「中性的没有」扩展到「有害的短缺」。

intro.en: Lack is a Middle English word for a gap or deficiency, and its earlier source is not fully settled.
intro.cn: lack 是中古英语中表示「缺口、不足」的词，更早的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Lak meant a deficiency, fault or want, and it was used both as a noun and as a verb.
items.cn: lak 意为不足、缺陷、匮乏，名词与动词两种用法都有。

items.en: Many dictionaries suggest a Middle Dutch or Middle Low German source with the same sense, but the path is uncertain.
items.cn: 多数词典推测它来自意义相同的中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，但具体路径并不确定。

items.en: The word is recorded in English from the twelfth century onward, always close to the idea of something missing.
items.cn: 这个词从十二世纪起见于英语文献，始终贴近「有东西缺失」的概念。

items.en: Early modern writers use lack for both material shortage and personal fault, widening its range.
items.cn: 近代早期作家用 lack 兼指物资短缺与人的缺点，词义范围随之扩大。

items.en: Modern English keeps the simple noun and verb and builds phrases such as for lack of and lack of sleep.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词与动词的基本用法，并形成 for lack of、lack of sleep 等搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the spelling or the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for absence and shortage.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同词干的词；近义组收表示「没有、短缺」的词。

entries.definition: Missing or not having enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少的；不足的。

entries.definition: Dull and without energy or brightness.
entries.definitionCN: 暗淡的；平淡无奇的。

entries.definition: A servant who obeys orders without question.
entries.definitionCN: 唯命是从的仆人；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To fall behind or a delay.
entries.definitionCN: 落后；滞后；只是拼写相近。

entries.definition: A situation in which there is not enough of something.
entries.definitionCN: 短缺；不足。

entries.definition: The state of something not being present.
entries.definitionCN: 缺席；不存在。

entries.definition: A lack of something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏；需要。

normalIntro.en: The word is short and blunt, and its few relatives all circle the idea of an empty place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短促直接，少数同族词都围绕「空着的位置」这一意思。

normal.en: Lack is both noun and verb with no change of shape: a lack of water, to lack water.
normal.cn: lack 名动同形：a lack of water 与 to lack water 都不加后缀。

normal.en: For lack of is a fixed phrase meaning 'because something is missing'.
normal.cn: for lack of 是固定搭配，意为「因为缺少某物」。

normal.en: Lacking adds -ing and works as an adjective: the lacking supplies.
normal.cn: lacking 加 -ing 作形容词：缺少的物资。

normal.en: Lackluster joins lack to luster, a word for shine.
normal.cn: lackluster 把 lack 与表示光泽的 luster 组合起来。

normal.en: The word never takes an article before the missing thing: lack of time, not lack of the time.
normal.cn: 说 lack of time，不说 lack of the time。

abstract.en: A word for a hole in a set of things reminds us that language can point at what is not there.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「一套东西里的空洞」的词，提醒人语言也能指向不在场的东西。

abstract.en: Because lack is neutral in shape, only context tells whether the gap is mild or dangerous.
abstract.cn: lack 本身是中性的，只有上下文才说明这个缺口是轻微还是危险。

abstract.en: Every shortage is measured against a standard that says how much should have been there.
abstract.cn: 每一种短缺都是对照「本该有多少」的标准量出来的。

examples.en: The cake failed because of a lack of flour.
examples.cn: 蛋糕因为面粉不够而做失败了。

examples.en: Many students lack confidence in speaking English.
examples.cn: 许多学生说英语时缺乏信心。

examples.en: There is no lack of volunteers for the event.
examples.cn: 这项活动的志愿者并不缺。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来克」——东西没来够克数，就是缺；lack 记作「缺」。

root: 中古英语 lak（不足、缺陷），更早来源一般推测为中古荷兰语或中古低地德语，具体路径来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an empty place where something should be; the senses move from a neutral absence to a verb and then to a harmful shortage.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「本该有东西的空位」；义项从「中性的没有」转到动词用法，再转到「有害的短缺」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty bowl on a table where food should have been.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摆着一只空碗，本该盛着食物。

branches.en: a pantry shelf with nothing on it
branches.cn: 空空如也的食品架

branches.en: a speaker searching for a word that will not come
branches.cn: 说话人找不到合适的词

branches.en: a village waiting for a water truck
branches.cn: 等水车来的村子

branches.en: the same gap, first seen and then suffered
branches.cn: 同一个缺口，先被看见，再让人吃苦

branches.en: a hand reaching for a tool that is not there
branches.cn: 伸手去拿却不存在的工具

intro.en: The word is a bare English stem with two common suffixes and one compound in its family.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个光裸的英语词干，同族里有两个常见后缀和一个复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的 -ing 后缀
构成过去式的 -ed 后缀

definition_zh: 包含；容纳；控制；抑制
definition_en: to have something inside, or to keep something under control
core_image: 一只箱子把里面的东西全兜住，一点不外漏
scene: 她打开信封，里面是一张折好的地图。 This box contains all the old letters.
sceneCN: 这里 contain 指「装有、包含」（第 1 个义项：内部盛有某物）；句意是这只箱子里装着所有旧信件。

senses.title: Have inside
senses.definition: to have something inside or as a part
senses.definitionCN: 内部盛有某物，或把某物作为一部分
senses.example: The letter contains a short apology.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信里有一句简短的道歉。
senses.why: A shell is interesting mainly for what it keeps.
senses.whyCN: 一个外壳之所以值得一提，主要看它装着什么。

senses.title: Have room for
senses.definition: to be able to hold a certain amount
senses.definitionCN: 能够装下一定的数量
senses.example: This bottle contains two litres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个瓶子能装两升。
senses.why: Every container has a limit it never tells you out loud.
senses.whyCN: 每个容器都有一个它不会开口说的限度。

senses.title: Keep under control
senses.definition: to stop something from spreading or showing
senses.definitionCN: 阻止某事物扩散或显露出来
senses.example: Firefighters contained the fire before midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 消防员在午夜前控制住了火势。
senses.why: The same word that holds water can hold back fear.
senses.whyCN: 兜住水的那同一个词，也能兜住恐惧。

intro.en: Contain comes from Latin continere, to hold together, built from com-, together, and tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: contain 来自拉丁语 continere，意为握在一起，由 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

items.en: Tenere meant to hold in the hand or keep.
items.cn: tenere 意为握在手中或守住。

items.en: Continere meant to hold things together inside.
items.cn: continere 意为把东西拢在里面。

items.en: It also meant to keep feelings or crowds in check.
items.cn: 它也指把情绪或人群约束住。

items.en: French contenir carried the holding sense into use.
items.cn: 法语 contenir 把盛装的含义带入使用。

items.en: English contain first meant to hold within limits.
items.cn: 英语 contain 最初指在界限内盛住。

items.en: It now covers both holding things and holding back danger.
items.cn: 如今它既指盛装物品，也指遏制危险。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin hold base ten-, and the meaning group names other verbs for having something inside.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语握持词基 ten-，近义组列出其他表示内部含有的动词。

entries.definition: an object made to hold things
entries.definitionCN: 容器；集装箱

entries.definition: what is inside something
entries.definitionCN: 内容；所含之物

entries.definition: to keep something in good condition
entries.definitionCN: 维持；保养

entries.definition: to have something inside or in your hand
entries.definitionCN: 容纳；握住

entries.definition: to have something as one of its parts
entries.definitionCN: 包括；包含

entries.definition: to be made up of particular parts
entries.definitionCN: 由…组成；包含

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a closed box, then move to a bottle with a fixed limit and to a fire held inside a line.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只合上的箱子开始，再到一个有固定容量的瓶子，最后到被拦在一条线里的火。

normal.en: Con- is together and tain is hold, so contain is holding things together inside.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，tain 是握住，contain 就是把东西拢在里面。

normal.en: A box contains, a bottle contains, a good speaker contains nerves.
normal.cn: 箱子装着东西，瓶子装着水，好的演讲者装着紧张。

normal.en: Contain is a wall; include is a welcome.
normal.cn: contain 是一道墙，include 是一声欢迎。

normal.en: The lid is closed, and the story stays inside.
normal.cn: 盖子合上，故事就留在里面。

normal.en: To contain a fire is to give it nowhere to go.
normal.cn: 控制一场火，就是让它无处可去。

abstract.en: Picture a closed tin on a high shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象高处架子上的一只合上的铁盒。

abstract.en: Picture a jar filled exactly to the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一只刚好装到刻线的罐子。

abstract.en: Picture a rope line stopping a crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳线拦住人群。

examples.en: The report contains several useful charts.
examples.cn: 这份报告里有几张有用的图表。

examples.en: This drink contains no sugar at all.
examples.cn: 这种饮料完全不含糖。

examples.en: Doctors worked fast to contain the infection.
examples.cn: 医生迅速行动以控制感染。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 contain 记成 con（一起）加 tain（握住）：把东西一起握在壳里，就是包含、容纳。

root: 源自拉丁语 continere（com 一起 + tenere 握住），本义是把东西拢在一起，后指包含、容纳与把危险或情绪控制住。

sensesIntro.en: From what a box keeps inside, to the amount a bottle can hold, and to a fire stopped at a line.
sensesIntro.cn: 从箱子里装着的东西，到瓶子能装的量，最后到被拦在一条线上的火。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed box with everything held inside its walls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只合上的箱子，东西都被兜在四壁之内。

branches.en: The first sense is simply what the walls enclose.
branches.cn: 第一个义项就是四壁围住的东西。

branches.en: The second sense is the size of the space inside.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是内部空间的大小。

branches.en: The third sense keeps something from getting out.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是让某物跑不出去。

branches.en: Both senses are about an inside that has a limit.
branches.cn: 两个义项都关于一个有界限的内部。

branches.en: A space with limits can also limit a danger.
branches.cn: 有界限的空间，也能限制危险。

intro.en: Contain is built on Latin com-, together, plus tenere, to hold.
intro.cn: contain 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 tenere（握住）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hold base ten-/tain- also appears in maintain, obtain and retain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的握持词基 ten-/tain- 也出现在 maintain、obtain 与 retain 中。

items.meaning: a thing made to hold other things
items.example: Put the rice in a container.

items.meaning: the act of keeping something in
items.meaningCN: 把某物限制在内的行为
items.example: The containment of the leak took hours.
items.exampleCN: 控制泄漏花了几个小时。

items.meaning: able to be kept under control
to keep holding in good state
items.meaningCN: 持续握住并保持良好状态
items.exampleCN: 他们把这条路养护得很好。

items.example: She obtained a copy of the file.
items.exampleCN: 她拿到了文件的一份副本。

definition_zh: 古典的；古希腊罗马的；古典音乐（传统）的；公认的
definition_en: belonging to ancient Greece and Rome, following a formal artistic tradition, or long established as standard
core_image: 石柱与三角山墙撑起的希腊神庙正面
scene: 音乐厅里调音完毕，观众安静下来。 The orchestra opened with a piece of classical music from Vienna.
sceneCN: 这里 classical 指「古典音乐（传统）的」（第 2 个义项：属于欧洲严肃音乐的正式传统）；句意是乐团以一首维也纳古典乐曲开场。

pos.zh: 古典的；古希腊罗马的；古典音乐的

senses.title: Of ancient Greece and Rome
senses.definition: belonging to the civilisation of ancient Greece and Rome
senses.definitionCN: 属于古希腊与古罗马文明的
senses.example: He reads classical texts in the original.
senses.exampleCN: 他读古典原著。
senses.why: The best writers of antiquity were the original classics, so their whole world became classical.
senses.whyCN: 上古最优秀的作家原本就是经典，于是他们的整个世界都被称为古典。

senses.title: Of a formal musical tradition
senses.definition: belonging to the serious European musical tradition from about seventeen fifty onwards
senses.definitionCN: 属于十八世纪中叶以来欧洲严肃音乐传统的
senses.example: She grew up listening to classical music.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小听古典音乐。
senses.why: Music that followed the old models of form and balance took the same label as ancient art.
senses.whyCN: 遵循旧有形式与均衡范本的音乐，借用了古代艺术的那个标签。

senses.title: Established as standard
senses.definition: long accepted as the standard form of a subject or method
senses.definitionCN: 长期被接受为某学科或方法的标准形式
senses.example: Classical physics fails at very small scales.
senses.exampleCN: 经典物理学在极小尺度上失效。
senses.why: What is taught as the old standard is called classical, in contrast with newer models.
senses.whyCN: 作为旧有标准被教授的内容被称为经典，以区别于更新的模型。

intro.en: Classical is the adjective of classic and keeps the idea of a first-rank model.
intro.cn: classical 是 classic 的形容词形式，保留了第一流范本的观念。

items.en: Classicus meant of the highest class.
items.cn: classicus 意为最高等级的。

items.en: The best authors were called scriptores classici.
items.cn: 最优秀的作家被称为 scriptores classici。

items.en: Classical first described the best Greek and Latin authors.
items.cn: classical 最初形容最优秀的希腊罗马作家。

items.en: The word spread to architecture, art and then music.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到建筑、艺术，随后又扩展到音乐。

items.en: It now also marks the older standard in science.
items.cn: 它如今也标记科学中的旧有标准。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the classic family, while the meaning group names old and standard traditions.
note.cn: 形近组列出 classic 家族，近义组列出古老与标准传统。

entries.definition: of lasting high quality or very typical
entries.definitionCN: 经久不衰的或非常典型的

entries.definition: a person who studies ancient texts
entries.definitionCN: 研究古代典籍的人

entries.definition: stylish and of good quality
entries.definitionCN: 有格调且品质好的

entries.definition: following customs handed down over time
entries.definitionCN: 遵循世代相传的习俗

entries.definition: belonging to the distant past
entries.definitionCN: 属于遥远过去的

entries.definition: following an official or strict style
entries.definitionCN: 遵循正式或严格风格的

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the ancient world, the concert hall and the standard science sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用古代世界、音乐厅与标准科学义。

normal.en: Classical is classic plus -al, so it always describes something rather than naming a work.
normal.cn: classical 是 classic 加 -al，因此总在形容某物，而不是指某部作品。

normal.en: A classic novel is a great book, while classical literature is the literature of Greece and Rome.
normal.cn: a classic novel 指一本好书，classical literature 则指希腊罗马文学。

normal.en: Classical music is a shelf in the record shop, not simply old music.
normal.cn: 古典音乐是唱片店里的一格分类，而不只是老音乐。

normal.en: Classical physics is the physics taught before relativity and quantum theory came along.
normal.cn: 经典物理指相对论与量子论出现之前所教的物理。

normal.en: The -al ending makes a word about a tradition, not about one admired example.
normal.cn: 后缀 -al 让词指向一种传统，而非某一件被称赏的作品。

abstract.en: Picture a marble temple front with six columns and a low triangle above.
abstract.cn: 想象一座六根石柱、上方有扁三角的大理石神庙正面。

abstract.en: Picture a string section tuning to a single note before the conductor arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥上台前弦乐组对着一个音调音。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard of old formulas still used in a modern lesson.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上写满如今课堂仍在使用的旧公式。

examples.en: He reads classical texts in the original.
examples.cn: 他读古典原著。

examples.en: The orchestra opened with a piece of classical music from Vienna.
examples.cn: 乐团以一首维也纳古典乐曲开场。

examples.en: Classical physics fails at very small scales.
examples.cn: 经典物理学在极小尺度上失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 classic 想成「一流」，al 想成「的」：属于一流传统的，就是古典的。

root: 源自拉丁语 classicus（最高等级的），由形容一流作家的用法扩展为形容古希腊罗马及其艺术传统。

sensesIntro.en: From the ancient world to its art, then to music, and finally to any established standard.
sensesIntro.cn: 从古代世界到其艺术，再到音乐，最后到任何既定标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marble temple front with balanced columns.
core.cn: 核心意象：比例匀称的石柱神庙正面。

branches.en: The top rank attaches to the ancient world itself.
branches.cn: 最高等级直接附着于古代世界。

branches.en: Music that follows old forms inherits the label.
branches.cn: 遵循旧形式的音乐继承了这个标签。

branches.en: An old standard stays classical beside newer models.
branches.cn: 旧标准在新模型旁仍称经典。

branches.en: Both rest on imitation of ancient models.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在模仿古代范本之上。

branches.en: Old age and high authority combine in one word.
branches.cn: 古老与权威在这个词里合而为一。

intro.en: The adjective adds -al to classic and grows a style noun, an agent noun and a prefix form.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由 classic 加 -al 构成，并长出风格名词、施动名词与前缀形式。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin classicus, so classical and classify share one rank word.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 classicus，因此 classical 与 classify 共用一个等级词。

items.example: The hall is built in a classical style.
items.exampleCN: 这座大厅按古典风格建造。

items.meaningCN: 以古代范本为基础的艺术
items.exampleCN: 这场运动转向古典主义。

items.meaning: a student of the ancient world
items.example: A classicist advised on the text.
items.exampleCN: 一位古典学者为文本提供了意见。

items.example: The bank has a neoclassical front.
items.exampleCN: 这家银行有座新古典风格的正面。

items.example: The car is a classic model.
Classical comes from the word for class.
items.exampleCN: classical 来自表示等级的那个词。

latinEntries.example: Classicus gave both classic and classical.
latinEntries.exampleCN: classicus 同时给出 classic 与 classical。

definition_zh: 不能的；不会的；无能力的
definition_en: lacking the skill, means or opportunity to do something
core_image: 想伸手去做，手却够不着那件东西
scene: 电话铃响到第四声，她刚做完手术的手还打着绷带，怎么也接不起来。 She was unable to lift the receiver after the operation.
sceneCN: 这里 unable 是形容词「不能的」（第 1 个义项：缺乏能力或条件去做某事）；句意为手术后她无法拿起听筒。

pos.zh: 形容词：不能的；不会的；无能力的（只作表语，不用于名词前）

collocations.zh: 遗憾地无法（委婉拒绝用语）

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「能力」，unable 即其否定形态的形容词
由 able 加副词后缀构成，义为「能干地」，与本词构成正反对照

senses.title: Lacking the power or skill to do something
senses.definition: not having the physical or mental power, or the skill, needed to do something
senses.definitionCN: 不具备做某事所需的体力、脑力或技能
senses.example: He was unable to walk without support after the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤后他无法独自行走。
senses.why: The core image is the missing arm of the scale: able carries a weight, unable cannot lift it.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是天平上缺失的一端：able 拿得起，unable 拿不起。

senses.title: Lacking the means or opportunity
senses.definition: not having the money, time, tools or circumstances required
senses.definitionCN: 不具备所需的钱、时间、工具或环境条件
senses.example: The family were unable to afford the school fees.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人负担不起学费。
senses.why: The hand that cannot reach is not always weak; sometimes the ladder itself is missing.
senses.whyCN: 够不着的手未必无力；有时缺的是梯子本身。

senses.title: Unable to attend: polite refusal
senses.definition: in invitations and replies, a polite formula for declining
senses.definitionCN: 在邀请与回复中，用于婉拒的礼貌套语
senses.example: I am sorry to say I shall be unable to attend the dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 很遗憾，我将无法出席晚宴。
senses.why: Inability is the politest form of no: the refusal is blamed on circumstances, not on will.
senses.whyCN: 「无法」是最体面的拒绝：把推辞归因于境况而非意愿。

senses.title: Unable to cope: overwhelmed
senses.definition: not having the resources or strength to manage a situation
senses.definitionCN: 没有足够的资源或力量去应对某个局面
senses.example: New parents often feel unable to cope at first.
senses.exampleCN: 新手父母起初常觉得应付不过来。
senses.why: The load exceeds the lifter; the same missing weight returns at the scale of life.
senses.whyCN: 负载超过承力者；天平上缺失的那端在生活的秤上重现。

senses.title: Unable to say or find words
senses.definition: not able to express something in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 无法用言语或文字表达某事
senses.example: She was unable to find the words for her grief.
senses.exampleCN: 她无法用语言形容自己的悲恸。
senses.why: Even expression is an act: what cannot be lifted into words stays heavy inside.
senses.whyCN: 表达也是一种「举」：举不进言辞之物沉重地留在心里。

senses.title: Unable to believe or accept
senses.definition: not able to accept a fact or idea as true
senses.definitionCN: 无法把某个事实或观念当作真实来接受
senses.example: They were unable to believe the news at first.
senses.exampleCN: 起初他们无法相信这个消息。
senses.why: Belief is a grip of the mind; what the mind cannot hold, it cannot accept.
senses.whyCN: 相信是心智的抓握；心智握不住的，便无法接受。

senses.title: Legally or officially unable
senses.definition: prevented by law, rule or contract from doing something
senses.definitionCN: 因法律、规则或合同限制而不能做某事
senses.example: The bank was unable by law to release the records.
senses.exampleCN: 依法银行不能公开这些档案。
senses.why: The ladder can be removed by rules as well as by weakness; prohibition is another missing rung.
senses.whyCN: 梯子既可因无力而缺，也可因规则而被抽走；禁令就是缺失的那一级。

senses.title: Unable to see or hear
senses.definition: lacking the sight or hearing needed to perceive something
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏看见或听见所需的感官能力
senses.example: From the back row they were unable to see the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 从后排他们看不见舞台。
senses.why: Perception is the reach of the senses; beyond that reach, the thing might as well not exist.
senses.whyCN: 感知是感官的「够」；超出够及之处，那东西形同不存在。

intro.en: Unable is the native prefix un- laid on the Old English adjective able.
intro.cn: unable 是在本族前缀 un- 加于古英语形容词 able 之上构成的。

items.en: *h2ebhlus is generally reconstructed as the source of the able family; the deeper trail is source uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为 able 词族可溯至重构形式 *h2ebhlus；更早的脉络不确定。

items.en: Old English had related forms such as ēaðel and habyl, meaning easy to be held or fit.
items.cn: 古英语有 ēaðel、habyl 等相关形式，意为「易于保有；合适的」。

items.en: The modern adjective came through Old French able, habilé, from Latin habilis 'easy to hold, fit'.
items.cn: 现代形容词经古法语 able、habilé 传入，源自拉丁语 habilis「易握的；合适的」。

items.en: Able was settled in Middle English with the sense of competent or capable.
items.cn: 十四世纪 able 在中古英语中定型，意为「有能力的」。

items.en: The negative unable appears early, building the opposite directly on the word.
items.cn: 否定式 unable 很早出现，直接在 able 之上构成反义。

items.en: Today unable is used only after a verb, chiefly as be unable to.
items.cn: 如今 unable 只用于动词之后，主要作 be unable to。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the un- family and the able family; the near-meaning group gathers cannot, incapable and lacking words.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 词族与 able 词族；近义组收 cannot、incapable 及表缺乏的词。

entries.definition: Having the skill, power or means; the positive word beneath the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能够的」，是本词去掉否定前缀后的正面词。

entries.definition: Not lessening; the un-a-b spelling pattern resembles unable without sharing its root.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不减弱的」，拼写模式与 unable 相似但词根不同。

entries.definition: Capably; the adverb of able, the positive mirror of unable.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「能干地」，able 的副词形式，与本词互为正反镜像。

entries.definition: Not normal; shares the letter a-b with able but comes from Latin ab- plus norma.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「异常的」，与 able 同含 a-b 字母组合，但源自拉丁语 ab- 加 norma。

entries.definition: Not able to be used or obtained; a longer sibling on the same able stem.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可用的；无法获得的」，是同一 able 词干上的较长同族词。

entries.definition: Not capable; more permanent in tone, often of persons or qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无能力的」，语气上更显持久，常指人或品质。

entries.definition: The direct verb form of being unable; shorter and plainer.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词否定式，义为「不能」，比 unable 更直接朴素。

entries.definition: Without power to act or change things; emphasizes strength and authority.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无能为力的」，强调力量与权柄的缺失。

entries.definition: Unable to act for oneself; adds the sense of needing help.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无助的；束手无策的」，兼具需要帮助之义。

entries.definition: Not suitable or qualified for a role; stresses fitness rather than momentary ability.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不胜任的；不合适的」，强调资格与适应，而非一时的能力。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real prefix structure and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的构词结构，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: Unable is un- plus able: put not in front of capable.
normal.cn: unable 就是 un- 加 able：在「能够」前面放一个「不」。

normal.en: Be unable to is the fixed frame: it never stands before a noun.
normal.cn: be unable to 是固定句型：它从不放在名词前。

normal.en: Unable to attend is the polite way to say no to an invitation.
normal.cn: unable to attend 是婉拒邀请的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Unable to cope means the load has grown past your strength.
normal.cn: unable to cope 意为负荷已超出你的承受力。

normal.en: Regrettably unable softens a refusal on paper.
normal.cn: regrettably unable 让书面回绝显得委婉。

abstract.en: Picture a hand stretched toward a shelf just beyond its reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向差一寸才够得着的书架。

abstract.en: Sometimes the hand is strong and the ladder is missing.
abstract.cn: 有时手很有力，缺的是那架梯子。

abstract.en: Some weights cannot be lifted; some words cannot be said.
abstract.cn: 有些重物举不起；有些话说不出。

examples.en: The airline was unable to confirm the connecting flight.
examples.cn: 航空公司无法确认转接航班。

examples.en: She was unable to hide her disappointment at the result.
examples.cn: 她无法掩饰对结果的失望。

examples.en: We regret we are unable to accept late submissions.
examples.cn: 很遗憾，我们不能接受逾期提交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安恩博」——安恩博举不动这块石头：不能

root: unable 由本族否定前缀 un- 加 able 构成；able 经古法语 able、habilé 来自拉丁语 habilis「易握的；合适的」；able 词族一般认为可溯至原始印欧语重构形式 *h2ebhlus；反义词为 able。

sensesIntro.en: The eight senses of unable all measure a gap between wish and reach: strength missing, means missing, polite refusal, overwhelm, silence, disbelief, prohibition, and the senses' own limits.
sensesIntro.cn: unable 的八个义项都在丈量愿望与够及之间的距离：缺力、缺条件、婉拒、应付不来、说不出、难以置信、依法不能，以及感官自身的限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaches for what it cannot grasp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向它握不住的东西。

branches.en: THE BODY: strength and the senses fall short of the task.
branches.cn: 身体线：力量与感官不足以完成任务。

branches.en: THE CONDITIONS: means and rules remove the ladder.
branches.cn: 条件线：手段与规则抽走了梯子。

branches.en: THE COURTESY: inability as the polite form of refusal.
branches.cn: 礼节线：以「无法」为体的婉拒。

branches.en: THE LOAD: when coping fails, the load has outgrown the lifter.
branches.cn: 负荷线：当应对失灵，负载已超过承受者。

branches.en: THE MIND: unspoken grief and disbelief are weights the mind cannot lift.
branches.cn: 心智线：说不出的悲恸与难以置信，都是心智举不起的重量。

intro.en: Unable is a clean two-part word: the negative prefix un- on the able stem.
intro.cn: unable 是个干净的两段式词：否定前缀 un- 加 able 词干。

latinIntro.en: The stem comes from Latin habilis through Old French; the prefix un- is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 词干经古法语源自拉丁语 habilis；前缀 un- 则是本族日耳曼语成分。

items.example: It is the Latin stem of able.
items.exampleCN: 它是 able 的拉丁词干。
它把 able 变为 unable。

items.example: It appears in comfortable, unbreakable and kin words.
items.exampleCN: 它见于 comfortable、unbreakable 等同族词。

items.example: It forms abnormal, a mere look-alike.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormal，与 unable 只是形近。

items.example: It forms incapable, the near synonym.

items.exampleCN: 它构成 powerless 与 helpless。

items.example: Cannot is the plain verb counterpart.
items.exampleCN: cannot 是其平实的动词对应形式。

derivatives.zh: 本词去掉否定前缀的正面形式，义为「能够的」

definition_zh: 代表；代理人；典型的；有代表性的
definition_en: a person chosen to speak or act for a group, or something that is typical of a larger whole
core_image: 会议室里写着「村民代表」的牌子前，坐着一个被大家推选出来的人
scene: 全国各地的代表聚到首都，把各自选区的声音带进会场。 Each representative carried the concerns of a different region.
sceneCN: 这里 representative 是「代表」（第 1 个义项：被选出替群体发言的人）；句意：每位代表都带来了不同地区的关切。

senses.title: A person chosen to act for others
senses.definition: someone who is chosen to speak or vote for a group of people
senses.definitionCN: 被选出替一群人发言或投票的人
senses.example: The union sent three representatives to the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 工会派了三名代表参加会谈。
senses.why: The -ative ending marks a person or thing that carries out the action of representing.
senses.whyCN: -ative 词尾标记执行「代表」这一动作的人或物。

senses.title: A typical example
senses.definition: typical of a group, so that it can be used as an example of the whole
senses.definitionCN: 能体现整个群体特征的，可作为整体的例子
senses.example: The survey used a representative sample of adults.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查使用了有代表性的成年人样本。
senses.why: If a person stands for a group, a sample can stand for a whole population in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个人能代表一个群体，一个样本也能以同样方式代表整个人群。

senses.title: Based on elected members
senses.definition: describing a system in which elected people make decisions for the public
senses.definitionCN: 描述由民选代表替公众作决定的制度
senses.example: The country has a representative government.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家实行代议制政府。
senses.why: A government made of representatives is simply the adjective form applied to a whole system.
senses.whyCN: 由代表组成的政府，只是把这个形容词用在整个制度上。

intro.en: Representative is formed inside English by adding -ative to represent, which comes from Latin repraesentare.
intro.cn: representative 是英语在 represent 后加 -ative 构成的，而 represent 来自拉丁语 repraesentare。

items.en: Repraesentare means to make present or bring before the eyes.
items.cn: repraesentare 意为使在场或带到眼前。

items.en: The ending -ativus marks something that performs or relates to an action.
items.cn: 词尾 -ativus 标记执行某动作或与之相关的事物。

items.en: Old French representer brings the verb into English.
items.cn: 古法语 representer 把动词带入英语。

items.en: Middle English uses representative for a person who stands for others.
items.cn: 中古英语用 representative 指替他人出场的人。

items.en: Political theory adopts representative for elected government.
items.cn: 政治理论采用 representative 指代议制政府。

items.en: Modern English extends it to samples and typical examples.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到样本和典型例子。

note.en: Representative is the person-or-adjective form of the represent family, and it is close to names for delegates and typical examples.
note.cn: representative 是 represent 词族中「人」或形容词的形态，与代表和典型例子的名称相邻。

entries.definition: to speak or act for others
entries.definitionCN: 代表；描绘

entries.definition: the act of representing
entries.definitionCN: 代表；表现

entries.definition: showing things as they appear
entries.definitionCN: 具象的

entries.definition: a person sent to speak or vote for a group
entries.definitionCN: 代表；会议代表

entries.definition: a person who acts for someone else
entries.definitionCN: 代理人

entries.definition: a person who speaks officially for a group
entries.definitionCN: 发言人

entries.definition: showing the usual qualities of a group
entries.definitionCN: 典型的

normalIntro.en: Representative contains represent plus -ative, and the ending signals either a person who represents or an adjective meaning typical.
normalIntro.cn: representative 由 represent 加 -ative 构成，词尾要么指「执行代表的人」，要么是形容词「典型的」。

normal.en: Represent plus -ative: a person who does the representing.
normal.cn: represent 加 -ative：执行代表动作的人。

normal.en: A sales representative is the person who stands for the company to customers.
normal.cn: sales representative 就是公司对客户出面的那个人。

normal.en: A representative sample stands for the whole population.
normal.cn: representative sample 代表整个人群。

normal.en: Elected representative makes the political role explicit.
normal.cn: elected representative 明确点出政治角色。

normal.en: Representative of can mean typical of as well as speaking for.
normal.cn: representative of 既可指「代表」，也可指「典型体现」。

abstract.en: Picture a name card on a long table, marking one seat as the village's seat.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上的一张名牌，把某个座位标为村子的座位。

abstract.en: Imagine one apple chosen to stand for a whole crate.
abstract.cn: 想象一个苹果被选出来代表整箱苹果。

abstract.en: Think of a spokesperson stepping up to a row of microphones.
abstract.cn: 想象发言人走到一排麦克风前。

examples.en: Each department elected a representative to the committee.
examples.cn: 每个部门都选了一名代表进入委员会。

examples.en: The study used a representative sample of students.
examples.cn: 这项研究使用了有代表性的学生样本。

examples.en: The painting is representative of his early style.
examples.cn: 这幅画代表了他的早期风格。

dict_mnemonic.text: represent（代表）+ -ative（人／形容词词尾）＝代表或典型的；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: represent（代表，源自拉丁语 repraesentare「使在场」）+ 词尾 -ative，表示执行代表动作的人，或具有代表性的事物。

sensesIntro.en: The person comes first, then the typical sample that stands for a whole, then the whole system built from such people.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是代人行事的人，再是代表整体的典型样本，最后是由这些人构成的整套制度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one chosen person or sample standing in for a larger whole.
core.cn: 核心意象：被选出的一个人或样本，代替更大的整体出场。

branches.en: The chosen person who speaks for others is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 被选出替他人发言的人，是基本义项。

branches.en: A sample can stand for a population just as a person stands for a group.
branches.cn: 样本代表总体，正如人代表群体。

branches.en: A whole system can be built out of elected representatives.
branches.cn: 整套制度可以由民选代表构成。

branches.en: Person and sample both work by standing in for something larger.
branches.cn: 人与样本都通过代替更大的事物来发挥作用。

branches.en: Elected individuals and representative government share the same political logic.
branches.cn: 民选个人与代议制政府共享同一套政治逻辑。

intro.en: Representative is an English adjective-and-noun form built on the Latin verb represent.
intro.cn: representative 是在拉丁动词 represent 基础上构成的英语形容词兼名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ending -ativus marks something that performs an action, so representative names the one who makes others present.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词尾 -ativus 标记执行动作的事物，所以 representative 指「使他人出场的人」。

items.example: Represent is the base of representative.
items.exampleCN: represent 是 representative 的基础词。
representative 由 represent 与 -ative 合成。
representation 共享 represent 词干。
representational 共享 represent 词干。
